# Dossier — Stage 3: change over time

The requirements from stages 1 and 2 continue to apply, with the additions below.
Numbered section references such as §4 and §8 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Companies change, and the web changes with them: a refresh may be served pages that earlier
builds were not, and may no longer be served pages they were. Sources also correct
themselves. A dossier now keeps the history of each field, answers as it stood at an earlier
time, and publishes its changes in a feed. It also names the company's executives.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

4. Every change to a selected value appears exactly once in the change feed, at the time this
   stage assigns to it.

## Two times per value

Every candidate and every selected value now has two times:

- **`true_from`**: the date from which the evidence says the value holds. A page states it
  in the header line `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>`. A page with no valid `Effective` line takes
  the date part, in UTC, of its `published_at`; with neither, `true_from` is null.
- **`learned_at`**: when this service first had the value. For a candidate, it is the time
  (§8, Builds) of the first build that gathered a candidate with the same field, value, URL
  and provider. For a selected value, it is the time of the build that made it the
  selected value.

Candidates gain `true_from` and `learned_at`. `retrieved_at` (stage 2) stays the time of the
build that gathered the candidate in the current candidate set. A selected value's
`true_from` is that of its selected candidate.

Each field of `GET /dossiers/{domain}` also carries the selected value's `true_from` and
`learned_at`. Both are null when the field is `unknown`. In an `as_of` response these
describe the selected value at that snapshot, using no later history.

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` is unchanged.

## Executives

A dossier has a seventh field, `executives`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after the six fields of §4. A research run (§4) still asks for the
six fields of §4 only.

Its value is an array with one object `{ "title": T, "name": N }` for each title below that
has a selected person, in the order `cfo`, `coo`, `cto`. These objects are the field's
**members**. When no title has a selected person, the value is null and the field is
`unknown`.

For Appendix A, each title is a field with these statement phrases and with the format and
normalisation of `ceo` (A.4, A.5), the title's own statement phrases taking the place of
those for `ceo`:

| Title | Statement phrases |
|---|---|
| `cfo` | `chief financial officer`, `CFO` |
| `coo` | `chief operating officer`, `COO` |
| `cto` | `chief technology officer`, `CTO` |

A candidate of `executives` is a candidate of one title: it carries `title` beside `value`,
and its `value` is the person's name. A research claim is never a candidate of
`executives`.

```json
{ "value": [ { "title": "cfo", "name": "Ana Silva" }, { "title": "cto", "name": "Ben Okafor" } ],
  "status": "known", "true_from": "2025-09-01", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/team",
                   "excerpt": "Ana Silva is the chief financial officer of Acme Robotics.",
                   "provider": "nimble" },
                 { "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
                   "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CTO: Ben Okafor.", "provider": "tavily" } ],
  "candidates": [ { "title": "cfo", "value": "Ana Silva", "...": "...", "selected": true },
                  { "title": "cto", "value": "Ben Okafor", "...": "...", "selected": true } ] }
```

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` runs separately over the candidates of each title.

- `selected` is true on the highest-ranked candidate of each title that has candidates, and
  false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate by title, in the order above, then in rank order.
- `citations` are, for each member in order, the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
  candidate with the member's title and name, in rank order.
- `status` is `unknown` when the value is null, `contested` when the candidates of some
  title carry two or more different names, and `known` otherwise.
- A candidate's `learned_at` is the time of the first build that gathered a candidate with
  the same title, name, URL and provider.
- A member's `true_from` is that of its title's selected candidate. The field's `true_from`
  is the latest of its members' `true_from`, or null when any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` chooses each title's person from the candidates at
  `true_at` and gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `executives` is typed by title, in place of the table in
Changes and corrections. A title **differs** between the earlier and the new value when
exactly one of them has a member with that title, or both have one and their names differ. A
differing title counts as a correction when both values have a member with that title, both
members' `true_from` are not null, and the new member's is on or before the earlier
member's. The entry is `correction` when every differing title counts as a correction, and
`change` otherwise.

The `data-testid` attributes of the screens in `stage-2.md` name only the six fields of §4:
`executives` takes none of them, and a screen that shows it does so with other markup. On
`/contested`, "no field is contested" means none of those six fields is.

## Changes and corrections

When a build completes `ready`, each field whose selected value differs from its selected
value before the build gets one history entry, and one feed entry, of one of two types:

| Type | When |
|---|---|
| `correction` | Both the earlier and the new value are not null, and the new value's `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's `true_from` |
| `change` | Every other difference, including a value appearing where there was none, a value disappearing, and either `true_from` being null |

A field's first selected value, set by the dossier's first build that completes `ready`,
gets a history entry of type `initial` and no feed entry. A field that is `unknown` after
that build gets its first entry when it first gets a value, and that entry is a `change`.

A build that completes with the same selected value for a field adds nothing for it, even
when its candidates, citations or `true_from` differ. A `failed` build adds nothing. Concurrent refreshes
of one dossier run one build (§8) and so add each entry once.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test?as_of=2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00
```

Returns the dossier as this service had it at `as_of`: the fields, candidates and
`researched_at` of the latest build that completed `ready` and whose time is at or before
`as_of`, decided by `learned_at`, never by `true_from`. `state` is `ready`. `spent_units` is
the total of the builds whose time is at or before `as_of`.

When several ready builds have the same time, return the last of them in build order.
This also applies when equivalent RFC 3339 timestamps use different offsets. The clock
need not advance between builds.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `as_of` is not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No build of the dossier completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |
| No dossier for the domain | 404 `not_found` |

Without `as_of`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}` is unchanged.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values?true_at=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test/values?true_at=2025-06-01&as_of=2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00
```

Returns, for each field, the value that the evidence this service had at `as_of` says held
on the date `true_at`. `as_of` defaults to the current time (§8).

A **page version** is what one ready build gathered from one URL: its candidates and its
`true_from`. The versions of a URL known at `as_of` are those gathered by ready builds whose
time is at or before `as_of`, taken in build order. Each version holds from its `true_from`.
When a later version of the same URL is gathered, it replaces every earlier version of that
URL whose `true_from` is on or after its own. The latest earlier version that it does not
replace stops holding on the later version's `true_from`. A version whose `true_from` is
null holds from no date, and a later version with a null `true_from` replaces every earlier
version of its URL. A gathered version with no candidates still replaces or ends earlier
versions by this rule.

The candidates **at `true_at`** are those of every version that holds on that date. Each
field's value is chosen from them by the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, and its
`true_from` is that of the chosen candidate.

```json
{ "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "true_at": "2025-06-01",
  "as_of": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "fields": { "ceo": { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
                       "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
              "...": "..." } }
```

A field with no candidate at `true_at` has `"value": null`, `"true_from": null`,
`"citations": []`. Citations are those of the candidates at `true_at` with the chosen value.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `true_at` missing or not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or `as_of` not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No dossier for the domain, or no build of it completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |

For state imported from an export, the builds and versions are those Upgrades gives.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history`

```json
{
  "domain": "acme-robotics.test",
  "fields": {
    "ceo": [
      { "type": "initial", "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
        "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
        "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
      { "type": "change", "value": "Lee Park", "true_from": "2026-03-20",
        "learned_at": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
        "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "tavily" } ] }
    ],
    "legal_name": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "hq_city": [],
    "founded_year": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "headcount_range": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "funding_total": [ { "...": "..." } ],

@[[b8d788a8-8bc7-49bc-9e05-1ca0d3dfc53a]] spec stage-3 requirements, part 2 of 2 (FINAL PART)

    "executives": [ { "...": "..." } ]
  }
}
```

- `fields` holds all seven fields. Each list is in the order the entries were added, oldest
  first.
- An entry's `value`, `true_from`, `learned_at` and `citations` are those of the selected
  value it records. An entry whose value is null has `"true_from": null` and
  `"citations": []`.
- No dossier for the domain is 404 `not_found`.

## `GET /changes`

```http
GET /changes?since=0&limit=50
```

```json
{
  "changes": [
    { "seq": 1, "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "field": "ceo", "type": "change",
      "from": "Dana Ruiz", "to": "Lee Park", "true_from": "2026-03-20",
      "learned_at": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

The feed holds every `change` and `correction` entry of every dossier.

- `seq` is a positive integer, unique across the feed, and larger for every later entry.
  Entries added by one build are numbered in the order of the fields in `stage-1.md` §4,
  then `executives`.
- `from` and `to` are the earlier and the new selected value, either of which may be null.
  `true_from` is the new value's. `learned_at` is the time of the build that added the
  entry.
- `since` defaults to 0 and lists only entries whose `seq` is greater than it. It is an
  integer, 0 or more. Entries are ordered by `seq` ascending.
- `limit` defaults to 50, range 1 to 200. `has_more` is true when entries exist beyond the
  last one returned.

## Upgrades

A stage-3 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 or stage-2
service. Every imported field that has a value gets one history entry of type `initial`,
with `learned_at` the dossier's `researched_at` and `true_from` null unless the exported
state records the dates that give it. The feed starts empty; the first build after import
compares its selected values with the imported ones. Existing tokens, dossiers and completed
idempotent responses survive the import as in `stage-1.md` §10, and the history and feed
of a stage-3 export survive a stage-3 import unchanged. So do its builds: after a
stage-3 import, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer as they did in the exporting service.

State imported from a stage-1 export counts as one build that completed `ready` at the
dossier's `researched_at`, and each imported candidate's URL as one version gathered by it;
imported candidates have `learned_at` equal to their `retrieved_at`. An `as_of` at or after
that time and before the next build returns the imported fields, and an earlier `as_of` is
404 `not_found`. An imported dossier whose `researched_at` is null answers every `as_of` with
404 `not_found` until a build completes.

State imported from a stage-2 export keeps the builds that the stage-2 service made, each
with its time, its outcome and its spending. Each of them that completed `ready` keeps the
candidates it gathered and, for each URL it gathered, one page version whose `true_from`
follows from that page's `Effective` and `Published` lines as that build gathered them
(Two times per value). State that the stage-2 service had itself imported counts as one
build that completed `ready` at the dossier's `researched_at`. `?as_of=`, `/values` and each
candidate's `learned_at` then answer as if this service had made those builds. History is
still one `initial` entry per field that has a value, as above, and an `as_of` response takes
each field's `learned_at` and `true_from` from that history (Two times per value).

An export of a stage-1 or stage-2 service has no `executives` candidates. After its import,
`executives` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the export,
and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it adds a
`change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes `ready`.

## Concurrency

Concurrent refreshes and reads must produce the same results as executing them one at a time
in some order. No change appears twice in the feed, and none is missing from it.

## Restarts

This row replaces the Disk row of the resource limits in `stage-1.md` §2:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Disk | the container's filesystem; it survives a container restart |

The container may be stopped abruptly at any time, with no warning and no time to finish what
the service is doing, and then started again. The sentence "State need not survive an
abrupt container restart" in `stage-1.md` §10 no longer applies. When no build is running
at the stop, the service answers after the restart exactly
as it did before the stop:

- Every account signs in with its password, and every bearer token is valid.
- Every dossier answers `GET /dossiers/{domain}`, with and without `as_of`,
  `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` and `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history` as before, and
  `GET /dossiers` lists the same dossiers.
- The change feed holds the same entries with the same `seq`. An entry added after the
  restart has a larger `seq` than every entry before it.
- A replay of a completed idempotent request answers as §7 requires.
- The clock reads the time it read before the stop until reset or `POST /_test/clock` moves
  it.

- **No build is recorded.** The dossier keeps its id, domain, exported state and fields, which are all unknown with no candidates. It has no history entries.
- **Spend is kept.** The exported spend becomes a starting baseline. Reading the dossier shows it, and later builds add to it.
- **Every `as_of` returns 404 until a later build succeeds.** Once one does, `as_of` answers again.

One decision the ruling didn't cover: I treat that baseline as spend from before any build. So once `as_of` answers again, its spend total includes it.

A new test imports a never-researched dossier with a spend of 7 and checks:
- the import succeeds and reading the dossier shows a spend of 7;
- every `as_of`, past or future, returns 404, as does the values endpoint;
- after a refresh succeeds, `as_of` answers and its spend includes the 7.

The same test runs for a dossier imported from a stage-1 export.

# Dossier — Stage 3: change over time

The requirements from stages 1 and 2 continue to apply, with the additions below.
Numbered section references such as §4 and §8 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Companies change, and the web changes with them: a refresh may be served pages that earlier
builds were not, and may no longer be served pages they were. Sources also correct
themselves. A dossier now keeps the history of each field, answers as it stood at an earlier
time, and publishes its changes in a feed. It also names the company's executives.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

4. Every change to a selected value appears exactly once in the change feed, at the time this
   stage assigns to it.

## Two times per value

Every candidate and every selected value now has two times:

- **`true_from`**: the date from which the evidence says the value holds. A page states it
  in the header line `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>`. A page with no valid `Effective` line takes
  the date part, in UTC, of its `published_at`; with neither, `true_from` is null.
- **`learned_at`**: when this service first had the value. For a candidate, it is the time
  (§8, Builds) of the first build that gathered a candidate with the same field, value, URL
  and provider. For a selected value, it is the time of the build that made it the
  selected value.

Candidates gain `true_from` and `learned_at`. `retrieved_at` (stage 2) stays the time of the
build that gathered the candidate in the current candidate set. A selected value's
`true_from` is that of its selected candidate.

Each field of `GET /dossiers/{domain}` also carries the selected value's `true_from` and
`learned_at`. Both are null when the field is `unknown`. In an `as_of` response these
describe the selected value at that snapshot, using no later history.

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` is unchanged.

## Executives

A dossier has a seventh field, `executives`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after the six fields of §4. A research run (§4) still asks for the
six fields of §4 only.

Its value is an array with one object `{ "title": T, "name": N }` for each title below that
has a selected person, in the order `cfo`, `coo`, `cto`. These objects are the field's
**members**. When no title has a selected person, the value is null and the field is
`unknown`.

For Appendix A, each title is a field with these statement phrases and with the format and
normalisation of `ceo` (A.4, A.5), the title's own statement phrases taking the place of
those for `ceo`:

| Title | Statement phrases |
|---|---|
| `cfo` | `chief financial officer`, `CFO` |
| `coo` | `chief operating officer`, `COO` |
| `cto` | `chief technology officer`, `CTO` |

A candidate of `executives` is a candidate of one title: it carries `title` beside `value`,
and its `value` is the person's name. A research claim is never a candidate of
`executives`.

```json
{ "value": [ { "title": "cfo", "name": "Ana Silva" }, { "title": "cto", "name": "Ben Okafor" } ],
  "status": "known", "true_from": "2025-09-01", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/team",
                   "excerpt": "Ana Silva is the chief financial officer of Acme Robotics.",
                   "provider": "nimble" },
                 { "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
                   "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CTO: Ben Okafor.", "provider": "tavily" } ],
  "candidates": [ { "title": "cfo", "value": "Ana Silva", "...": "...", "selected": true },
                  { "title": "cto", "value": "Ben Okafor", "...": "...", "selected": true } ] }
```

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` runs separately over the candidates of each title.

- `selected` is true on the highest-ranked candidate of each title that has candidates, and
  false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate by title, in the order above, then in rank order.
- `citations` are, for each member in order, the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
  candidate with the member's title and name, in rank order.
- `status` is `unknown` when the value is null, `contested` when the candidates of some
  title carry two or more different names, and `known` otherwise.
- A candidate's `learned_at` is the time of the first build that gathered a candidate with
  the same title, name, URL and provider.
- A member's `true_from` is that of its title's selected candidate. The field's `true_from`
  is the latest of its members' `true_from`, or null when any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` chooses each title's person from the candidates at
  `true_at` and gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `executives` is typed by title, in place of the table in
Changes and corrections. A title **differs** between the earlier and the new value when
exactly one of them has a member with that title, or both have one and their names differ. A
differing title counts as a correction when both values have a member with that title, both
members' `true_from` are not null, and the new member's is on or before the earlier
member's. The entry is `correction` when every differing title counts as a correction, and
`change` otherwise.

The `data-testid` attributes of the screens in `stage-2.md` name only the six fields of §4:
`executives` takes none of them, and a screen that shows it does so with other markup. On
`/contested`, "no field is contested" means none of those six fields is.

## Changes and corrections

When a build completes `ready`, each field whose selected value differs from its selected
value before the build gets one history entry, and one feed entry, of one of two types:

| Type | When |
|---|---|
| `correction` | Both the earlier and the new value are not null, and the new value's `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's `true_from` |
| `change` | Every other difference, including a value appearing where there was none, a value disappearing, and either `true_from` being null |

A field's first selected value, set by the dossier's first build that completes `ready`,
gets a history entry of type `initial` and no feed entry. A field that is `unknown` after
that build gets its first entry when it first gets a value, and that entry is a `change`.

A build that completes with the same selected value for a field adds nothing for it, even
when its candidates, citations or `true_from` differ. A `failed` build adds nothing. Concurrent refreshes
of one dossier run one build (§8) and so add each entry once.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test?as_of=2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00
```

Returns the dossier as this service had it at `as_of`: the fields, candidates and
`researched_at` of the latest build that completed `ready` and whose time is at or before
`as_of`, decided by `learned_at`, never by `true_from`. `state` is `ready`. `spent_units` is
the total of the builds whose time is at or before `as_of`.

When several ready builds have the same time, return the last of them in build order.
This also applies when equivalent RFC 3339 timestamps use different offsets. The clock
need not advance between builds.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `as_of` is not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No build of the dossier completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |
| No dossier for the domain | 404 `not_found` |

Without `as_of`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}` is unchanged.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values?true_at=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test/values?true_at=2025-06-01&as_of=2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00
```

Returns, for each field, the value that the evidence this service had at `as_of` says held
on the date `true_at`. `as_of` defaults to the current time (§8).

A **page version** is what one ready build gathered from one URL: its candidates and its
`true_from`. The versions of a URL known at `as_of` are those gathered by ready builds whose
time is at or before `as_of`, taken in build order. Each version holds from its `true_from`.
When a later version of the same URL is gathered, it replaces every earlier version of that
URL whose `true_from` is on or after its own. The latest earlier version that it does not
replace stops holding on the later version's `true_from`. A version whose `true_from` is
null holds from no date, and a later version with a null `true_from` replaces every earlier
version of its URL. A gathered version with no candidates still replaces or ends earlier
versions by this rule.

The candidates **at `true_at`** are those of every version that holds on that date. Each
field's value is chosen from them by the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, and its
`true_from` is that of the chosen candidate.

```json
{ "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "true_at": "2025-06-01",
  "as_of": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "fields": { "ceo": { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
                       "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
              "...": "..." } }
```

A field with no candidate at `true_at` has `"value": null`, `"true_from": null`,
`"citations": []`. Citations are those of the candidates at `true_at` with the chosen value.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `true_at` missing or not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or `as_of` not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No dossier for the domain, or no build of it completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |

For state imported from an export, the builds and versions are those Upgrades gives.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history`

```json
{
  "domain": "acme-robotics.test",
  "fields": {
    "ceo": [
      { "type": "initial", "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
        "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
        "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
      { "type": "change", "value": "Lee Park", "true_from": "2026-03-20",
        "learned_at": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
        "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "tavily" } ] }
    ],
    "legal_name": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "hq_city": [],
    "founded_year": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "headcount_range": [ { "...": "..." } ],
    "funding_total": [ { "...": "..." } ],

@[[42dcdeaf-6e11-4624-b620-7766b6084e53]] spec stage-3 requirements, part 2 of 2 (FINAL PART)

    "executives": [ { "...": "..." } ]
  }
}
```

- `fields` holds all seven fields. Each list is in the order the entries were added, oldest
  first.
- An entry's `value`, `true_from`, `learned_at` and `citations` are those of the selected
  value it records. An entry whose value is null has `"true_from": null` and
  `"citations": []`.
- No dossier for the domain is 404 `not_found`.

## `GET /changes`

```http
GET /changes?since=0&limit=50
```

```json
{
  "changes": [
    { "seq": 1, "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "field": "ceo", "type": "change",
      "from": "Dana Ruiz", "to": "Lee Park", "true_from": "2026-03-20",
      "learned_at": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

The feed holds every `change` and `correction` entry of every dossier.

- `seq` is a positive integer, unique across the feed, and larger for every later entry.
  Entries added by one build are numbered in the order of the fields in `stage-1.md` §4,
  then `executives`.
- `from` and `to` are the earlier and the new selected value, either of which may be null.
  `true_from` is the new value's. `learned_at` is the time of the build that added the
  entry.
- `since` defaults to 0 and lists only entries whose `seq` is greater than it. It is an
  integer, 0 or more. Entries are ordered by `seq` ascending.
- `limit` defaults to 50, range 1 to 200. `has_more` is true when entries exist beyond the
  last one returned.

## Upgrades

A stage-3 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 or stage-2
service. Every imported field that has a value gets one history entry of type `initial`,
with `learned_at` the dossier's `researched_at` and `true_from` null unless the exported
state records the dates that give it. The feed starts empty; the first build after import
compares its selected values with the imported ones. Existing tokens, dossiers and completed
idempotent responses survive the import as in `stage-1.md` §10, and the history and feed
of a stage-3 export survive a stage-3 import unchanged. So do its builds: after a
stage-3 import, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer as they did in the exporting service.

State imported from a stage-1 export counts as one build that completed `ready` at the
dossier's `researched_at`, and each imported candidate's URL as one version gathered by it;
imported candidates have `learned_at` equal to their `retrieved_at`. An `as_of` at or after
that time and before the next build returns the imported fields, and an earlier `as_of` is
404 `not_found`. An imported dossier whose `researched_at` is null answers every `as_of` with
404 `not_found` until a build completes.

State imported from a stage-2 export keeps the builds that the stage-2 service made, each
with its time, its outcome and its spending. Each of them that completed `ready` keeps the
candidates it gathered and, for each URL it gathered, one page version whose `true_from`
follows from that page's `Effective` and `Published` lines as that build gathered them
(Two times per value). State that the stage-2 service had itself imported counts as one
build that completed `ready` at the dossier's `researched_at`. `?as_of=`, `/values` and each
candidate's `learned_at` then answer as if this service had made those builds. History is
still one `initial` entry per field that has a value, as above, and an `as_of` response takes
each field's `learned_at` and `true_from` from that history (Two times per value).

An export of a stage-1 or stage-2 service has no `executives` candidates. After its import,
`executives` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the export,
and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it adds a
`change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes `ready`.

## Concurrency

Concurrent refreshes and reads must produce the same results as executing them one at a time
in some order. No change appears twice in the feed, and none is missing from it.

## Restarts

This row replaces the Disk row of the resource limits in `stage-1.md` §2:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Disk | the container's filesystem; it survives a container restart |

The container may be stopped abruptly at any time, with no warning and no time to finish what
the service is doing, and then started again. The sentence "State need not survive an
abrupt container restart" in `stage-1.md` §10 no longer applies. When no build is running
at the stop, the service answers after the restart exactly
as it did before the stop:

- Every account signs in with its password, and every bearer token is valid.
- Every dossier answers `GET /dossiers/{domain}`, with and without `as_of`,
  `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` and `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history` as before, and
  `GET /dossiers` lists the same dossiers.
- The change feed holds the same entries with the same `seq`. An entry added after the
  restart has a larger `seq` than every entry before it.
- A replay of a completed idempotent request answers as §7 requires.
- The clock reads the time it read before the stop until reset or `POST /_test/clock` moves
  it.

  the date part, in UTC, of its `published_at`; with neither, `true_from` is null.
- **`learned_at`**: when this service first had the value. For a candidate, it is the time
  (§8, Builds) of the first build that gathered a candidate with the same field, value, URL
  and provider. For a selected value, it is the time of the build that made it the
  selected value.

Candidates gain `true_from` and `learned_at`. `retrieved_at` (stage 2) stays the time of the
build that gathered the candidate in the current candidate set. A selected value's
`true_from` is that of its selected candidate.

Each field of `GET /dossiers/{domain}` also carries the selected value's `true_from` and
`learned_at`. Both are null when the field is `unknown`. In an `as_of` response these
describe the selected value at that snapshot, using no later history.

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` is unchanged.

## Executives

A dossier has a seventh field, `executives`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after the six fields of §4. A research run (§4) still asks for the
six fields of §4 only.

Its value is an array with one object `{ "title": T, "name": N }` for each title below that
has a selected person, in the order `cfo`, `coo`, `cto`. These objects are the field's
**members**. When no title has a selected person, the value is null and the field is
`unknown`.

For Appendix A, each title is a field with these statement phrases and with the format and
normalisation of `ceo` (A.4, A.5), the title's own statement phrases taking the place of
those for `ceo`:

| Title | Statement phrases |
|---|---|
| `cfo` | `chief financial officer`, `CFO` |
| `coo` | `chief operating officer`, `COO` |
| `cto` | `chief technology officer`, `CTO` |

A candidate of `executives` is a candidate of one title: it carries `title` beside `value`,
and its `value` is the person's name. A research claim is never a candidate of
`executives`.

```json
{ "value": [ { "title": "cfo", "name": "Ana Silva" }, { "title": "cto", "name": "Ben Okafor" } ],
  "status": "known", "true_from": "2025-09-01", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/team",
                   "excerpt": "Ana Silva is the chief financial officer of Acme Robotics.",
                   "provider": "nimble" },
                 { "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
                   "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CTO: Ben Okafor.", "provider": "tavily" } ],
  "candidates": [ { "title": "cfo", "value": "Ana Silva", "...": "...", "selected": true },
                  { "title": "cto", "value": "Ben Okafor", "...": "...", "selected": true } ] }
```

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` runs separately over the candidates of each title.

- `selected` is true on the highest-ranked candidate of each title that has candidates, and
  false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate by title, in the order above, then in rank order.
- `citations` are, for each member in order, the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
  candidate with the member's title and name, in rank order.
- `status` is `unknown` when the value is null, `contested` when the candidates of some
  title carry two or more different names, and `known` otherwise.
- A candidate's `learned_at` is the time of the first build that gathered a candidate with
  the same title, name, URL and provider.
- A member's `true_from` is that of its title's selected candidate. The field's `true_from`
  is the latest of its members' `true_from`, or null when any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` chooses each title's person from the candidates at
  `true_at` and gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `executives` is typed by title, in place of the table in
Changes and corrections. A title **differs** between the earlier and the new value when
exactly one of them has a member with that title, or both have one and their names differ. A
differing title counts as a correction when both values have a member with that title, both
members' `true_from` are not null, and the new member's is on or before the earlier
member's. The entry is `correction` when every differing title counts as a correction, and
`change` otherwise.

The `data-testid` attributes of the screens in `stage-2.md` name only the six fields of §4:
`executives` takes none of them, and a screen that shows it does so with other markup. On
`/contested`, "no field is contested" means none of those six fields is.

## Changes and corrections

When a build completes `ready`, each field whose selected value differs from its selected
value before the build gets one history entry, and one feed entry, of one of two types:

| Type | When |
|---|---|
| `correction` | Both the earlier and the new value are not null, and the new value's `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's `true_from` |
| `change` | Every other difference, including a value appearing where there was none, a value disappearing, and either `true_from` being null |

A field's first selected value, set by the dossier's first build that completes `ready`,
gets a history entry of type `initial` and no feed entry. A field that is `unknown` after
that build gets its first entry when it first gets a value, and that entry is a `change`.

A build that completes with the same selected value for a field adds nothing for it, even
when its candidates, citations or `true_from` differ. A `failed` build adds nothing. Concurrent refreshes
of one dossier run one build (§8) and so add each entry once.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test?as_of=2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00
```

Returns the dossier as this service had it at `as_of`: the fields, candidates and
`researched_at` of the latest build that completed `ready` and whose time is at or before
`as_of`, decided by `learned_at`, never by `true_from`. `state` is `ready`. `spent_units` is
the total of the builds whose time is at or before `as_of`.

When several ready builds have the same time, return the last of them in build order.
This also applies when equivalent RFC 3339 timestamps use different offsets. The clock
need not advance between builds.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `as_of` is not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No build of the dossier completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |
| No dossier for the domain | 404 `not_found` |

Without `as_of`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}` is unchanged.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values?true_at=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test/values?true_at=2025-06-01&as_of=2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00
```

Returns, for each field, the value that the evidence this service had at `as_of` says held
on the date `true_at`. `as_of` defaults to the current time (§8).

A **page version** is what one ready build gathered from one URL: its candidates and its
`true_from`. The versions of a URL known at `as_of` are those gathered by ready builds whose
time is at or before `as_of`, taken in build order. Each version holds from its `true_from`.
When a later version of the same URL is gathered, it replaces every earlier version of that
URL whose `true_from` is on or after its own. The latest earlier version that it does not
replace stops holding on the later version's `true_from`. A version whose `true_from` is
null holds from no date, and a later version with a null `true_from` replaces every earlier
version of its URL. A gathered version with no candidates still replaces or ends earlier
versions by this rule.

The candidates **at `true_at`** are those of every version that holds on that date. Each
field's value is chosen from them by the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, and its
`true_from` is that of the chosen candidate.

```json
{ "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "true_at": "2025-06-01",
  "as_of": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "fields": { "ceo": { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
                       "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
              "...": "..." } }
```

A field with no candidate at `true_at` has `"value": null`, `"true_from": null`,
`"citations": []`. Citations are those of the candidates at `true_at` with the chosen value.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `true_at` missing or not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or `as_of` not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No dossier for the domain, or no build of it completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |

For state imported from an export, the builds and versions are those Upgrades gives.

## `GET /changes`

```http
GET /changes?since=0&limit=50
```

```json
{
  "changes": [
    { "seq": 1, "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "field": "ceo", "type": "change",

  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

The feed holds every `change` and `correction` entry of every dossier.

- `seq` is a positive integer, unique across the feed, and larger for every later entry.
  Entries added by one build are numbered in the order of the fields in `stage-1.md` §4,
  then `executives`.
- `from` and `to` are the earlier and the new selected value, either of which may be null.
  `true_from` is the new value's. `learned_at` is the time of the build that added the
  entry.
- `since` defaults to 0 and lists only entries whose `seq` is greater than it. It is an
  integer, 0 or more. Entries are ordered by `seq` ascending.
- `limit` defaults to 50, range 1 to 200. `has_more` is true when entries exist beyond the
  last one returned.

## Upgrades

A stage-3 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 or stage-2
service. Every imported field that has a value gets one history entry of type `initial`,
with `learned_at` the dossier's `researched_at` and `true_from` null unless the exported
state records the dates that give it. The feed starts empty; the first build after import
compares its selected values with the imported ones. Existing tokens, dossiers and completed
idempotent responses survive the import as in `stage-1.md` §10, and the history and feed
of a stage-3 export survive a stage-3 import unchanged. So do its builds: after a
stage-3 import, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer as they did in the exporting service.

State imported from a stage-1 export counts as one build that completed `ready` at the
dossier's `researched_at`, and each imported candidate's URL as one version gathered by it;
imported candidates have `learned_at` equal to their `retrieved_at`. An `as_of` at or after
that time and before the next build returns the imported fields, and an earlier `as_of` is
404 `not_found`. An imported dossier whose `researched_at` is null answers every `as_of` with
404 `not_found` until a build completes.

State imported from a stage-2 export keeps the builds that the stage-2 service made, each
with its time, its outcome and its spending. Each of them that completed `ready` keeps the
candidates it gathered and, for each URL it gathered, one page version whose `true_from`
follows from that page's `Effective` and `Published` lines as that build gathered them
(Two times per value). State that the stage-2 service had itself imported counts as one
build that completed `ready` at the dossier's `researched_at`. `?as_of=`, `/values` and each
candidate's `learned_at` then answer as if this service had made those builds. History is
still one `initial` entry per field that has a value, as above, and an `as_of` response takes
each field's `learned_at` and `true_from` from that history (Two times per value).

An export of a stage-1 or stage-2 service has no `executives` candidates. After its import,
`executives` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the export,
and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it adds a
`change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes `ready`.

## Concurrency

Concurrent refreshes and reads must produce the same results as executing them one at a time
in some order. No change appears twice in the feed, and none is missing from it.

## Restarts

This row replaces the Disk row of the resource limits in `stage-1.md` §2:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Disk | the container's filesystem; it survives a container restart |

The container may be stopped abruptly at any time, with no warning and no time to finish what
the service is doing, and then started again. The sentence "State need not survive an
abrupt container restart" in `stage-1.md` §10 no longer applies. When no build is running
at the stop, the service answers after the restart exactly
as it did before the stop:

- Every account signs in with its password, and every bearer token is valid.
- Every dossier answers `GET /dossiers/{domain}`, with and without `as_of`,
  `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` and `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history` as before, and
  `GET /dossiers` lists the same dossiers.
- The change feed holds the same entries with the same `seq`. An entry added after the
  restart has a larger `seq` than every entry before it.
- A replay of a completed idempotent request answers as §7 requires.
- The clock reads the time it read before the stop until reset or `POST /_test/clock` moves
  it.

## Architecture

```
handlers (unchanged shape) --> Store (in-memory, read path)

- **Write rule (E3-5):** each mutating handler validates, then runs

  catch-all returns the error envelope.
- **Reads** come from memory, which mirrors the DB.
- **Reset and import** run one transaction that deletes every row and inserts the new state,

From this folder:

```sh

{"args":{"content":""""Candidates from one page's browser text (stage-2 "Candidates", stage-3 "Executives").

Every value a page supports for a field is one candidate of that field for that page. Its
excerpt is the first sentence of the page (in page order) that supports that value. A value
supported for an executive title is a candidate of `executives` carrying that title. Every
candidate of a page has the page's `true_from` date.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from app.executives import EXECUTIVES
from app.pages import page_kind, page_true_from, published_at
from app.selection import Candidate, value_key
from app.support import TITLES, candidates as supported


def from_page(url: str, text: str, provider: str, domain: str,
              retrieved_at: str | None) -> list[Candidate]:
    kind = page_kind(url, text, domain)
    published = published_at(text)
    true_from = page_true_from(text, published)
    found: dict[tuple[str, str], Candidate] = {}
    for support in supported(text, domain):
        key = (support.field, value_key(support.value))
        if key in found:
            continue
        title = support.field if support.field in TITLES else None
        found[key] = Candidate(EXECUTIVES if title else support.field, support.value, url,
                               support.excerpt, provider, kind, published, retrieved_at,
                               true_from=true_from, title=title)
    return list(found.values())

class MockAdmin:
    """Optional mock-web call log/fault API, enabled only when the harness exposes it."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.url = os.environ.get("DOSSIER_MOCK_URL", "").rstrip("/")
        self.token = os.environ.get("DOSSIER_MOCK_TOKEN", "")
        self.enabled = bool(self.url and self.token)

    def request(self, method: str, path: str, *, json_body: dict | None = None) -> dict | None:
        if not self.enabled:
            return None
        response = requests.request(method, self.url + path,
                                    headers={"X-Mock-Admin": self.token},
                                    json=json_body, timeout=10)
        assert response.status_code in (200, 204), response.text
        return response.json() if response.content else None

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.request("POST", "/_mock/reset", json_body={"epoch": 0})

    def fault(self, provider: str, methods: list[str], mode: str) -> None:
        self.request("POST", "/_mock/faults", json_body={"provider": provider,
                                                              "methods": methods,
                                                              "mode": mode})

    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
        answer = self.request("GET", "/_mock/log")
        return answer["calls"] if answer else []

def test_as_of_instant_ties_choose_last_build_and_include_all_spend(api: API, token: str) -> None:
    first, _ = create_build(api, token)
    first_spend = first["spent_units"]
    # The test clock deliberately remains unchanged, so this ready refresh ties the first build.
    second, _ = refresh_build(api, token)
    assert parse_instant(first["researched_at"]) == parse_instant(second["researched_at"])
    instant_utc = quote("2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", safe="")
    equivalent_offset = quote("2026-03-01T14:30:00+05:30", safe="")
    at_utc = api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}?as_of={instant_utc}", token=token)
    at_offset = api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}?as_of={equivalent_offset}", token=token)
    assert at_utc.status_code == 200, at_utc.text
    assert at_offset.status_code == 200, at_offset.text
    assert at_utc.json()["fields"] == second["fields"]
    assert at_offset.json()["fields"] == second["fields"]
    assert at_utc.json()["spent_units"] == second["spent_units"]
    assert second["spent_units"] >= first_spend

    before = api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}?as_of=2026-03-01T08%3A59%3A59%2B00%3A00",
                     token=token)
    assert before.status_code == 404, before.text
    assert before.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_found"

def test_simultaneous_executive_title_changes_are_one_aggregate_entry(api: API, token: str) -> None:
    """T23/E3-7: executives is one field entry even when multiple titles differ."""
    first, _ = create_build(api, token)
    first_exec = first["fields"]["executives"]["value"]
    if not first_exec or len(first_exec) < 2:
        import pytest
        pytest.skip("the configured corpus has fewer than two selected executive titles")
    # A refresh over the fixed mock corpus is a safe public operation; this assertion is
    # conditional on it producing more than one changed title in the suite's corpus.
    set_clock(api, "2026-03-01T09:01:00+00:00")
    second, _ = refresh_build(api, token)
    second_exec = second["fields"]["executives"]["value"]
    old = {member["title"]: member["name"] for member in first_exec}
    new = {member["title"]: member["name"] for member in second_exec or []}
    differing = [title for title in ("cfo", "coo", "cto") if old.get(title) != new.get(title)]
    if len(differing) < 2:
        import pytest
        pytest.skip("the fixed corpus did not change multiple executive titles in one refresh")
    entries = history(api, token, TEST_DOMAIN)["fields"]["executives"]
    matching = [entry for entry in entries if entry["value"] == second_exec]
    assert len(matching) == 1
    assert matching[0]["value"] == second_exec
    all_feed = feed(api, token)["changes"]
    exec_feed = [entry for entry in all_feed if entry["field"] == "executives"]
    assert exec_feed and exec_feed[-1]["to"] == second_exec
    assert exec_feed[-1]["field"] == "executives"

# Dossier — Stage 3: change over time

The requirements from stages 1 and 2 continue to apply, with the additions below.
Numbered section references such as §4 and §8 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Companies change, and the web changes with them: a refresh may be served pages that earlier
builds were not, and may no longer be served pages they were. Sources also correct
themselves. A dossier now keeps the history of each field, answers as it stood at an earlier
time, and publishes its changes in a feed. It also names the company's executives.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

4. Every change to a selected value appears exactly once in the change feed, at the time this
   stage assigns to it.

## Two times per value

Every candidate and every selected value now has two times:

- **`true_from`**: the date from which the evidence says the value holds. A page states it
  in the header line `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>`. A page with no valid `Effective` line takes
  the date part, in UTC, of its `published_at`; with neither, `true_from` is null.
- **`learned_at`**: when this service first had the value. For a candidate, it is the time
  (§8, Builds) of the first build that gathered a candidate with the same field, value, URL
  and provider. For a selected value, it is the time of the build that made it the
  selected value.

Candidates gain `true_from` and `learned_at`. `retrieved_at` (stage 2) stays the time of the
build that gathered the candidate in the current candidate set. A selected value's
`true_from` is that of its selected candidate.

Each field of `GET /dossiers/{domain}` also carries the selected value's `true_from` and
`learned_at`. Both are null when the field is `unknown`. In an `as_of` response these
describe the selected value at that snapshot, using no later history.

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` is unchanged.

## Executives

A dossier has a seventh field, `executives`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after the six fields of §4. A research run (§4) still asks for the
six fields of §4 only.

Its value is an array with one object `{ "title": T, "name": N }` for each title below that
has a selected person, in the order `cfo`, `coo`, `cto`. These objects are the field's
**members**. When no title has a selected person, the value is null and the field is
`unknown`.

For Appendix A, each title is a field with these statement phrases and with the format and
normalisation of `ceo` (A.4, A.5), the title's own statement phrases taking the place of
those for `ceo`:

| Title | Statement phrases |
|---|---|
| `cfo` | `chief financial officer`, `CFO` |
| `coo` | `chief operating officer`, `COO` |
| `cto` | `chief technology officer`, `CTO` |

A candidate of `executives` is a candidate of one title: it carries `title` beside `value`,
and its `value` is the person's name. A research claim is never a candidate of
`executives`.

```json
{ "value": [ { "title": "cfo", "name": "Ana Silva" }, { "title": "cto", "name": "Ben Okafor" } ],
  "status": "known", "true_from": "2025-09-01", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/team",
                   "excerpt": "Ana Silva is the chief financial officer of Acme Robotics.",
                   "provider": "nimble" },
                 { "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
                   "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CTO: Ben Okafor.", "provider": "tavily" } ],
  "candidates": [ { "title": "cfo", "value": "Ana Silva", "...": "...", "selected": true },
                  { "title": "cto", "value": "Ben Okafor", "...": "...", "selected": true } ] }
```

The selection rule in `stage-2.md` runs separately over the candidates of each title.

- `selected` is true on the highest-ranked candidate of each title that has candidates, and
  false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate by title, in the order above, then in rank order.
- `citations` are, for each member in order, the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
  candidate with the member's title and name, in rank order.
- `status` is `unknown` when the value is null, `contested` when the candidates of some
  title carry two or more different names, and `known` otherwise.
- A candidate's `learned_at` is the time of the first build that gathered a candidate with
  the same title, name, URL and provider.
- A member's `true_from` is that of its title's selected candidate. The field's `true_from`
  is the latest of its members' `true_from`, or null when any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` chooses each title's person from the candidates at
  `true_at` and gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `executives` is typed by title, in place of the table in
Changes and corrections. A title **differs** between the earlier and the new value when
exactly one of them has a member with that title, or both have one and their names differ. A
differing title counts as a correction when both values have a member with that title, both
members' `true_from` are not null, and the new member's is on or before the earlier
member's. The entry is `correction` when every differing title counts as a correction, and
`change` otherwise.

The `data-testid` attributes of the screens in `stage-2.md` name only the six fields of §4:
`executives` takes none of them, and a screen that shows it does so with other markup. On
`/contested`, "no field is contested" means none of those six fields is.

## Changes and corrections

When a build completes `ready`, each field whose selected value differs from its selected
value before the build gets one history entry, and one feed entry, of one of two types:

| Type | When |
|---|---|
| `correction` | Both the earlier and the new value are not null, and the new value's `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's `true_from` |
| `change` | Every other difference, including a value appearing where there was none, a value disappearing, and either `true_from` being null |

A field's first selected value, set by the dossier's first build that completes `ready`,
gets a history entry of type `initial` and no feed entry. A field that is `unknown` after
that build gets its first entry when it first gets a value, and that entry is a `change`.

A build that completes with the same selected value for a field adds nothing for it, even
when its candidates, citations or `true_from` differ. A `failed` build adds nothing. Concurrent refreshes
of one dossier run one build (§8) and so add each entry once.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}?as_of=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test?as_of=2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00
```

Returns the dossier as this service had it at `as_of`: the fields, candidates and
`researched_at` of the latest build that completed `ready` and whose time is at or before
`as_of`, decided by `learned_at`, never by `true_from`. `state` is `ready`. `spent_units` is
the total of the builds whose time is at or before `as_of`.

When several ready builds have the same time, return the last of them in build order.
This also applies when equivalent RFC 3339 timestamps use different offsets. The clock
need not advance between builds.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `as_of` is not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No build of the dossier completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |
| No dossier for the domain | 404 `not_found` |

Without `as_of`, `GET /dossiers/{domain}` is unchanged.

## `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values?true_at=`

```http
GET /dossiers/acme-robotics.test/values?true_at=2025-06-01&as_of=2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00
```

Returns, for each field, the value that the evidence this service had at `as_of` says held
on the date `true_at`. `as_of` defaults to the current time (§8).

A **page version** is what one ready build gathered from one URL: its candidates and its
`true_from`. The versions of a URL known at `as_of` are those gathered by ready builds whose
time is at or before `as_of`, taken in build order. Each version holds from its `true_from`.
When a later version of the same URL is gathered, it replaces every earlier version of that
URL whose `true_from` is on or after its own. The latest earlier version that it does not
replace stops holding on the later version's `true_from`. A version whose `true_from` is
null holds from no date, and a later version with a null `true_from` replaces every earlier
version of its URL. A gathered version with no candidates still replaces or ends earlier
versions by this rule.

The candidates **at `true_at`** are those of every version that holds on that date. Each
field's value is chosen from them by the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, and its
`true_from` is that of the chosen candidate.

```json
{ "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "true_at": "2025-06-01",
  "as_of": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "fields": { "ceo": { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "true_from": "2021-04-01",
                       "citations": [ { "url": "...", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ] },
              "...": "..." } }
```

A field with no candidate at `true_at` has `"value": null`, `"true_from": null`,
`"citations": []`. Citations are those of the candidates at `true_at` with the chosen value.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `true_at` missing or not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or `as_of` not an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset | 422 `validation_failed` |
| No dossier for the domain, or no build of it completed `ready` with a time at or before `as_of` | 404 `not_found` |

For state imported from an export, the builds and versions are those Upgrades gives.

- `fields` holds all seven fields. Each list is in the order the entries were added, oldest

## `GET /changes`

```http
GET /changes?since=0&limit=50
```

```json
{
  "changes": [
    { "seq": 1, "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "field": "ceo", "type": "change",
      "from": "Dana Ruiz", "to": "Lee Park", "true_from": "2026-03-20",
      "learned_at": "2026-04-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

The feed holds every `change` and `correction` entry of every dossier.

- `seq` is a positive integer, unique across the feed, and larger for every later entry.
  Entries added by one build are numbered in the order of the fields in `stage-1.md` §4,
  then `executives`.
- `from` and `to` are the earlier and the new selected value, either of which may be null.
  `true_from` is the new value's. `learned_at` is the time of the build that added the
  entry.
- `since` defaults to 0 and lists only entries whose `seq` is greater than it. It is an
  integer, 0 or more. Entries are ordered by `seq` ascending.
- `limit` defaults to 50, range 1 to 200. `has_more` is true when entries exist beyond the
  last one returned.

## Upgrades

A stage-3 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 or stage-2
service. Every imported field that has a value gets one history entry of type `initial`,
with `learned_at` the dossier's `researched_at` and `true_from` null unless the exported
state records the dates that give it. The feed starts empty; the first build after import
compares its selected values with the imported ones. Existing tokens, dossiers and completed
idempotent responses survive the import as in `stage-1.md` §10, and the history and feed
of a stage-3 export survive a stage-3 import unchanged. So do its builds: after a
stage-3 import, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer as they did in the exporting service.

State imported from a stage-1 export counts as one build that completed `ready` at the
dossier's `researched_at`, and each imported candidate's URL as one version gathered by it;
imported candidates have `learned_at` equal to their `retrieved_at`. An `as_of` at or after
that time and before the next build returns the imported fields, and an earlier `as_of` is
404 `not_found`. An imported dossier whose `researched_at` is null answers every `as_of` with
404 `not_found` until a build completes.

State imported from a stage-2 export keeps the builds that the stage-2 service made, each
with its time, its outcome and its spending. Each of them that completed `ready` keeps the
candidates it gathered and, for each URL it gathered, one page version whose `true_from`
follows from that page's `Effective` and `Published` lines as that build gathered them
(Two times per value). State that the stage-2 service had itself imported counts as one
build that completed `ready` at the dossier's `researched_at`. `?as_of=`, `/values` and each
candidate's `learned_at` then answer as if this service had made those builds. History is
still one `initial` entry per field that has a value, as above, and an `as_of` response takes
each field's `learned_at` and `true_from` from that history (Two times per value).

An export of a stage-1 or stage-2 service has no `executives` candidates. After its import,
`executives` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the export,
and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it adds a
`change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes `ready`.

## Concurrency

Concurrent refreshes and reads must produce the same results as executing them one at a time
in some order. No change appears twice in the feed, and none is missing from it.

## Restarts

This row replaces the Disk row of the resource limits in `stage-1.md` §2:

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Disk | the container's filesystem; it survives a container restart |

The container may be stopped abruptly at any time, with no warning and no time to finish what
the service is doing, and then started again. The sentence "State need not survive an
abrupt container restart" in `stage-1.md` §10 no longer applies. When no build is running
at the stop, the service answers after the restart exactly
as it did before the stop:

- Every account signs in with its password, and every bearer token is valid.
- Every dossier answers `GET /dossiers/{domain}`, with and without `as_of`,
  `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` and `GET /dossiers/{domain}/history` as before, and
  `GET /dossiers` lists the same dossiers.
- The change feed holds the same entries with the same `seq`. An entry added after the
  restart has a larger `seq` than every entry before it.
- A replay of a completed idempotent request answers as §7 requires.
- The clock reads the time it read before the stop until reset or `POST /_test/clock` moves
  it.

- one build that completed `ready` at `researched_at`, holding all exported candidates;
- the whole `spent_units` charged to that build;
- a dossier whose `researched_at` is null has no ready build, so every `as_of` gives 404;
- the exported `state` stays the dossier's current outcome.

- an `as_of` before `researched_at` gives 404 even if stage 2 had earlier ready builds;

## Architecture

```
handlers (unchanged shape) --> Store (in-memory, read path)
                         \--> db.py (SQLite, WAL, synchronous=FULL; write path)
build.py --commit--> one transaction: build row + versions + dossier fields + history + feed + seq
startup: db.load() -> Store; health is 200 only after the load
```

- **Durable store (lead note, T67-T74):** SQLite through the stdlib `sqlite3`, so no new
  dependency. The file is `/srv/data/dossier.db`. The Dockerfile creates `/srv/data` and
  chowns it to the runtime user `dossier`, because `/srv` is root-owned (lead ruling; builder
  notes R4).
  - Settings: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=FULL; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`.
  - Tables: `meta(key, value)` (clock, clock_set, seq), `users`, `tokens`, `dossiers`,
    `builds(dossier_id, build_no, time, outcome, spent, fields_json, candidates_json)`,
    `versions(dossier_id, build_no, url, true_from, candidates_json)`,
    `history(dossier_id, field, n, entry_json)`,
    `feed(seq PRIMARY KEY, dossier_id, entry_json)`,
    `idempotency(user_id, method, path, key, fingerprint, status, body_json)`.
- **Write rule (E3-5):** each mutating handler validates, then runs
  `with db.tx(): write rows`. The commit (fsync under `synchronous=FULL`) happens before the
  in-memory update and before the response. There is no `await` inside, so on one event loop
  this keeps §11 serialisability. A failed commit raises before memory changes, and the
  catch-all returns the error envelope.
- **Reads** come from memory, which mirrors the DB.
- **Reset and import** run one transaction that deletes every row and inserts the new state,
  then swap memory and bump the generation.

{"is_error":false,"name":"Bash","output":"# Dossier service — stage 3

An HTTP service and browser app that researches companies by web domain and keeps a
cited profile (a dossier) for each: six fields plus the company's executives (CFO, COO, CTO),
with every candidate value its sources support and one selected per field. Each dossier keeps
the history of its fields, answers as it stood at an earlier time (`?as_of=`) and what held on
a date (`/values?true_at=`), and publishes its changes in a feed (`/changes`). Python 3.12,
Starlette on uvicorn, state in SQLite on the container's filesystem. Every provider call goes
through WebRouter (`webrouter`, module `web_router`) to Nimble.

## Build and start

From this folder:

```sh
docker build -t dossier-stage-3 . && docker run --name dossier -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 \
  -e NIMBLE_API_KEY -e NIMBLE_BASE_URL dossier-stage-3
```

- `PORT` (default `8080`) is the port the service listens on, on `0.0.0.0`.
- `NIMBLE_API_KEY` is the Nimble credential. It is read from the environment by WebRouter and
  never stored or logged by the service.
- `NIMBLE_BASE_URL` is the Nimble endpoint. Leave it unset for the live endpoint
  (`https://sdk.nimbleway.com`); never set it to an empty string, which breaks every call.
- `TAVILY_API_KEY` / `TAVILY_BASE_URL`, `KERNEL_API_KEY` / `KERNEL_BASE_URL` and
  `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` / `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL` may be passed but are not used: the service
  researches with Nimble alone and reads every page through Nimble's rendered extract.

Open `http://localhost:8080/` in a browser, sign up, and research a domain.

`GET /health` answers `{"status": "ok"}` once the service is up (a few seconds).

State lives in `/srv/data/dossier.db` (SQLite in WAL mode, `synchronous=FULL`) on the
container's filesystem, created in the image and owned by the runtime user `dossier`. Every
change is committed to disk before its response is sent, so after `docker kill dossier` and
`docker start dossier` the service answers as before: accounts, tokens, dossiers, builds,
history, the change feed, completed idempotent requests and the clock. A build running at the
stop is dropped; its dossier keeps its last completed state. No volume is needed (removing the
container with `docker rm` removes its state). `DATA_DIR` (default `/srv/data`) moves the
database directory, for running outside the image.

| `app/dossiers.py`, `app/idempotency.py` | Dossier endpoints and `Idempotency-Key` handling |
| `app/store.py`, `app/db.py` | In-memory state the handlers read; the SQLite file every change is written to first |
| `app/clock.py`, `app/domains.py`, `app/http.py`, `app/errors.py` | Clock, domain rules, request/response helpers |
| `app/build.py`, `app/budget.py` | Background builds: searches and research, then rendered page reads, the 80-unit cap |

from app.db import Writer
from app.fields import decide
from app.history import entries_for_build, first_seen, stamp_candidates, stamp_fields
from app.selection import Candidate
from app.store import BuildRecord, Dossier, State


def record_build(state: State, dossier: Dossier, writer: Writer, time: str, spent_units: int,
                 candidates: list[Candidate] | None, pages: list[dict]) -> None:
    """Record a build of ``dossier`` at ``time``: failed when ``candidates`` is None, else
    ready with those candidates, gathered from ``pages`` ([{url, true_from}])."""
    number = len(dossier.builds) + 1
    dossier.spent_units += spent_units
    if candidates is None:
        build = BuildRecord(number, time, "failed", spent_units)
        dossier.outcome = "failed"
    else:
        ready_before = dossier.ready_builds()
        seen = first_seen([b.fields for b in ready_before])
        fields = stamp_fields(decide(stamp_candidates(candidates, seen, time)),
                              dossier.fields, time)
        for name, entry, change in entries_for_build(dossier.fields, fields,
                                                     not ready_before, time):
            dossier.history[name].append(entry)
            writer.add_history(dossier.id, name, entry)
            if change is not None:
                change = {"seq": state.next_seq(), "domain": dossier.domain, **change}
                state.feed.append(change)
                writer.add_feed(change)
        build = BuildRecord(number, time, "ready", spent_units, fields, pages)
        dossier.fields = fields
        dossier.outcome = "ready"
        dossier.researched_at = time
    dossier.builds.append(build)
    writer.add_build(dossier.id, build)
    writer.put_dossier(dossier)

import threading


class Log:
    """A thread-safe, append-only list of call entries."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._calls = []

    def record(self, provider, method, *, cost, status, **entry):
        """Append one call; optional `depth`, `query`, `max_results`, `fields`, `urls`,
        `session` (a browser session's id) and `served` (url, text) pairs."""
        served = entry.get("served", ())
        with self._lock:
            self._calls.append({
                "seq": len(self._calls) + 1, "provider": provider, "method": method,
                "depth": entry.get("depth"), "query": entry.get("query"),
                "max_results": entry.get("max_results"), "fields": entry.get("fields"),
                "urls": list(entry.get("urls", ())), "session": entry.get("session"),
                "cost": cost, "status": status,
                "served": [{"url": url, "text": text} for url, text in served]})

    def calls(self):
        """Every entry, oldest first."""
        with self._lock:
            return list(self._calls)

    def clear(self):
        """Forget every entry; numbering starts again at 1."""
        with self._lock:
            self._calls.clear()

def from_page(url: str, text: str, provider: str, domain: str,
              retrieved_at: str | None) -> list[Candidate]:
    kind = page_kind(url, text, domain)
    published = published_at(text)
    true_from = page_true_from(text, published)
    found: dict[tuple[str, str], Candidate] = {}
    for support in supported(text, domain):
        key = (support.field, value_key(support.value))
        if key in found:
            continue
        title = support.field if support.field in TITLES else None
        found[key] = Candidate(EXECUTIVES if title else support.field, support.value, url,
                               support.excerpt, provider, kind, published, retrieved_at,
                               true_from=true_from, title=title)
    return list(found.values())

Each write handler parses and authenticates first, then runs one synchronous critical
section (no ``await``): idempotency lookup, validation, the state change and the stored
response. That makes concurrent requests behave as if run one at a time (§7, §11).

from __future__ import annotations

from starlette.requests import Request

from app import idempotency, timeline
from app.auth import authenticate
from app.clock import format_time, parse_rfc3339
from app.domains import normalise
from app.errors import invalid, not_found
from app.fields import ALL_FIELDS
from app.http import json_response, query_int, query_text, read_json_object, require_str
from app.pages import parse_date
from app.store import Dossier

_REFRESH_FINGERPRINT = idempotency.fingerprint({})


def _path_domain(request: Request) -> str:
    return normalise(request.path_params["domain"])


async def create(services, request: Request):
    store, builds, clock = services.store, services.builds, services.clock
    user_id = authenticate(store, request)
    key = idempotency.require_key(request)
    body = await read_json_object(request)
    build_time = clock.now()
    # critical section
    state = store.state
    known = {"domain": body["domain"]} if "domain" in body else {}
    print_ = idempotency.fingerprint(known)
    record = idempotency.record_key(user_id, request, key)
    replayed = idempotency.replay(state, record, print_)
    if replayed is not None:
        return replayed
    domain = normalise(require_str(body, "domain"))
    dossier = state.dossiers.get(domain)
    with store.transaction() as writer:
        if dossier is not None:
            return idempotency.remember(state, writer, record, print_, 200, dossier.summary())
        dossier = Dossier(state.new_id("d"), domain)
        writer.put_dossier(dossier)
        state.dossiers[domain] = dossier
        builds.start(dossier, build_time)
        return idempotency.remember(state, writer, record, print_, 202, dossier.summary())


async def refresh(services, request: Request):
    store, builds, clock = services.store, services.builds, services.clock
    user_id = authenticate(store, request)
    key = idempotency.require_key(request)
    build_time = clock.now()
    # critical section; the body is ignored entirely (§7)
    state = store.state
    record = idempotency.record_key(user_id, request, key)
    replayed = idempotency.replay(state, record, _REFRESH_FINGERPRINT)
    if replayed is not None:
        return replayed
    dossier = state.dossiers.get(_path_domain(request))
    if dossier is None:
        raise not_found("no dossier for that domain")
    with store.transaction() as writer:
        if dossier.build is None:

    first, _ = create_build(api, token)

    if not first_exec or len(first_exec) < 2:
        import pytest
        pytest.skip("the configured corpus has fewer than two selected executive titles")
    # A refresh over the fixed mock corpus is a safe public operation; this assertion is

    second, _ = refresh_build(api, token)
    second_exec = second["fields"]["executives"]["value"]
    old = {member["title"]: member["name"] for member in first_exec}
    new = {member["title"]: member["name"] for member in second_exec or []}
    differing = [title for title in ("cfo", "coo", "cto") if old.get(title) != new.get(title)]

        import pytest
        pytest.skip("the fixed corpus did not change multiple executive titles in one refresh")
