An HTTP service and browser app that researches companies by web domain and keeps a
cited profile (a dossier) for each: six fields plus the company's executives (CFO, COO, CTO),
with every candidate value its sources support and one selected per field. Each dossier keeps
the history of its fields, answers as it stood at an earlier time (`?as_of=`) and what held on
a date (`/values?true_at=`), and publishes its changes in a feed (`/changes`). Python 3.12,
Starlette on uvicorn, state in SQLite on the container's filesystem. Every provider call goes
through WebRouter (`webrouter`, module `web_router`) to Nimble.

## Build and start

From this folder:

```sh
docker build -t dossier-stage-3 . && docker run --name dossier -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 \
  -e NIMBLE_API_KEY -e NIMBLE_BASE_URL dossier-stage-3
```

- `PORT` (default `8080`) is the port the service listens on, on `0.0.0.0`.
- `NIMBLE_API_KEY` is the Nimble credential. It is read from the environment by WebRouter and
  never stored or logged by the service.
- `NIMBLE_BASE_URL` is the Nimble endpoint. Leave it unset for the live endpoint
  (`https://sdk.nimbleway.com`); never set it to an empty string, which breaks every call.
- `TAVILY_API_KEY` / `TAVILY_BASE_URL`, `KERNEL_API_KEY` / `KERNEL_BASE_URL` and
  `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` / `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL` may be passed but are not used: the service
  researches with Nimble alone and reads every page through Nimble's rendered extract.

Open `http://localhost:8080/` in a browser, sign up, and research a domain.

`GET /health` answers `{"status": "ok"}` once the service is up (a few seconds).

State lives in `/srv/data/dossier.db` (SQLite in WAL mode, `synchronous=FULL`) on the
container's filesystem, created in the image and owned by the runtime user `dossier`. Every
change is committed to disk before its response is sent, so after `docker kill dossier` and
`docker start dossier` the service answers as before: accounts, tokens, dossiers, builds,
history, the change feed, completed idempotent requests and the clock. A build running at the
stop is dropped; its dossier keeps its last completed state. No volume is needed (removing the
container with `docker rm` removes its state). `DATA_DIR` (default `/srv/data`) moves the
database directory, for running outside the image.

@[[a8fd21aa-c149-4b38-94cd-d081b8102554]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 1 of 3

# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

## Investors

A dossier has an eighth field, `investors`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after `executives`, and the feed entries one build adds are
numbered with `investors` last.

For Appendix A, `investors` is a field with the statement phrases `investor`, `investors`,
`led by`, `backed by` and `participated`. Occurrences of the company's name and of these
statement phrases are first taken out of the sentence and separate the words around them.
Of the runs of capitalised words (A.4) joined by single spaces that remain, each not part of
a longer such run, a run of two or more words whose last word is `Ventures`, `Capital`,

@[[a8fd21aa-c149-4b38-94cd-d081b8102554]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 2 of 3

`Partners`, `Fund`, `Investments`, `Holdings` or `Equity` is an **investor name**. In an
excerpt that contains an amount (A.4), the run that starts directly after `led by` or
`backed by` and one space is an investor name too, whatever its length and last word:
`Acme Robotics raised $40M in a round led by General Atlantic.` names `General Atlantic`,
and `Acme Robotics is led by Dana Ruiz.` names no investor. An
investor name normalises to the text as the excerpt writes it. Rules 1 to 4 of A.2 apply;
in place of rule 5, an excerpt supports each investor name it contains.

The `value` of a candidate of `investors` is one investor name. A research claim is never a
candidate of `investors`.

An investor name is a **member** when, among the field's candidates, one with that name has
`kind` `own` or `filing`, or those with that name have two or more distinct origins.

In place of the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, the value is the array of the members'
names, sorted by Unicode code point, or null when there is no member. `investors` is `known`
exactly when it has a member, and `unknown` otherwise, in place of the rules that make a
field `known` exactly when the evidence supports a value for it.

```json
{ "value": ["Bluebird Capital", "Northwind Ventures"], "status": "known",
  "true_from": "2024-05-02", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "candidates": [ { "value": "Bluebird Capital", "...": "...", "selected": true }, { "...": "..." } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "dealwire.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `selected` is true on every candidate whose name is a member, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate in the order the selection rule in `stage-2.md` ranks
  them.
- `citations` are, for each member in the order of the value, the `url`, `excerpt` and
  `provider` of every candidate with its name, in rank order.
- A member's `true_from` is the earliest `true_from` that is not null among the candidates
  with its name, or null when all of them are null. The field's `true_from` is the latest of
  its members' `true_from`, or null when the value is null or any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` decides membership from the candidates at `true_at` and
  gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `investors` is typed by name, in place of the table in
`stage-3.md` Changes and corrections. A name in the new value and not in the earlier one
counts as a correction when its `true_from` and the earlier value's `true_from` are both not
null and its `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's. The entry is `correction` when
every name in exactly one of the two values counts as a correction, and `change` otherwise.

The screens treat `investors` as `stage-3.md` treats `executives`: it takes none of the
`data-testid` attributes of `stage-2.md`, and "no field is contested" on `/contested` means
none of the six fields of §4 is.

## Batches

`POST /batches` starts builds, and so joins `POST /dossiers` and
`POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` as a request that makes provider calls (§8, Builds).

A batch researches several companies under one shared budget. A batch belongs to the user who
created it; another user's batch is 404 `not_found`.

### `POST /batches`

**An idempotent write path.** `Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /batches
Idempotency-Key: 5d02e1...

{ "domains": ["acme-robotics.test", "brightgear.test"], "budget_units": 200 }
```

```json
202
{ "batch_id": "b_2", "state": "running", "budget_units": 200, "spent_units": 0,
  "dossiers": [ { "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "state": "building" },
                { "domain": "brightgear.test", "state": "ready" } ] }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `domains` missing, empty or longer than 50 entries | 422 `validation_failed` |
| An entry of `domains` invalid after normalisation (§4) | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Two entries of `domains` the same after normalisation | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `budget_units` missing, not an integer, below 1 or above 100000 | 422 `validation_failed` |

A `budget_units` that is not an integer is 422 `validation_failed` whatever its JSON type: a
string, `true` or `1.5` included. The row above takes precedence over the 400
`malformed_request` of §5 for a field of the wrong JSON type.

- `dossiers` lists the normalised domains in the order given, each with its dossier's state.
- A domain with no dossier gets one, and the batch runs its first build. A domain that
  already has a dossier is not researched by the batch and costs it nothing.
- `spent_units` is the total cost (§9) of the provider calls the batch's builds made. It never
  exceeds `budget_units`. Each build in a batch still spends at most 80 units, and its cost
  also counts in its dossier's `spent_units`.
- When the budget would be exceeded by a further call, the batch makes no more provider calls,
  and its remaining builds complete with the pages and research claims they have obtained:
  each of their fields is `known` exactly when those support a value for it.

### `GET /batches/{id}`

Returns the batch in the shape above. `state` is `running` while any of its builds runs, then
`done`. Unknown batch is 404 `not_found`.

## Provider failure

A provider may answer a call with an error (any 5xx status, or 429). The build continues: it
may make the same request again, through that provider or another.

@[[a8fd21aa-c149-4b38-94cd-d081b8102554]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 3 of 3 (FINAL PART)


- A build in which every call to one or more providers fails, while `nimble` answers,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence (§4) reachable through the
  providers that answer supports.
- A build in which every research run fails, while searches and extracts are answered,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence reachable by search and
  extract supports.
- A build in which every call to every provider fails completes `failed` (§8), within the
  time bound of §8.
- A call a provider refuses with an error status costs nothing (§9).

## Restarts

The restart requirements of `stage-3.md` hold for batches as for the rest of the state. When
builds are running at the stop, everything else is still answered as before the stop, and
each build that was running:

- Does not stay `building`. It ends `ready` or `failed` within 10 seconds of `GET /health`
  first answering 200 after the restart, when each provider call it makes after the restart
  answers within one second. It may end `failed` although some of its calls succeeded; it
  then leaves the fields as they were (§8).
- Is one build across the restart: its calls before and after the stop together spend at
  most 80 units (§9), and a batch's builds together never spend more than its
  `budget_units`.
- Has every unit a provider billed for its calls, before and after the stop, counted in its
  dossier's `spent_units` and, for a batch's build, in the batch's `spent_units`. They may
  also count calls that were in flight at the stop and that no provider billed.

After the restart, `POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` starts a new build of each such dossier
as it does for any other.

## Upgrades

A stage-4 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3
service, preserving dossiers, candidates, history, the change feed and completed idempotent
responses as in `stage-1.md` §10. A stage-3 export keeps its
builds: after the upgrade, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer from them as the stage-3 service did,
with the keys this stage adds. Citations carried in the
imported state remain citations served to this service.

An export of a stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3 service has no `investors` candidates. After its
import, `investors` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the
export, and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it
adds a `change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes
`ready`.

# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

## Investors

A dossier has an eighth field, `investors`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after `executives`, and the feed entries one build adds are
numbered with `investors` last.

For Appendix A, `investors` is a field with the statement phrases `investor`, `investors`,
`led by`, `backed by` and `participated`. Occurrences of the company's name and of these
statement phrases are first taken out of the sentence and separate the words around them.
Of the runs of capitalised words (A.4) joined by single spaces that remain, each not part of
a longer such run, a run of two or more words whose last word is `Ventures`, `Capital`,

An investor name is a **member** when, among the field's candidates, one with that name has

In place of the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, the value is the array of the members'

  "true_from": "2024-05-02", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",

## Batches

`POST /batches` starts builds, and so joins `POST /dossiers` and
`POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` as a request that makes provider calls (§8, Builds).

A batch researches several companies under one shared budget. A batch belongs to the user who
created it; another user's batch is 404 `not_found`.

### `POST /batches`

**An idempotent write path.** `Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /batches
Idempotency-Key: 5d02e1...

{ "domains": ["acme-robotics.test", "brightgear.test"], "budget_units": 200 }
```

```json
202
{ "batch_id": "b_2", "state": "running", "budget_units": 200, "spent_units": 0,
  "dossiers": [ { "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "state": "building" },
                { "domain": "brightgear.test", "state": "ready" } ] }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `domains` missing, empty or longer than 50 entries | 422 `validation_failed` |
| An entry of `domains` invalid after normalisation (§4) | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Two entries of `domains` the same after normalisation | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `budget_units` missing, not an integer, below 1 or above 100000 | 422 `validation_failed` |

A `budget_units` that is not an integer is 422 `validation_failed` whatever its JSON type: a
string, `true` or `1.5` included. The row above takes precedence over the 400
`malformed_request` of §5 for a field of the wrong JSON type.

- `dossiers` lists the normalised domains in the order given, each with its dossier's state.
- A domain with no dossier gets one, and the batch runs its first build. A domain that
  already has a dossier is not researched by the batch and costs it nothing.
- `spent_units` is the total cost (§9) of the provider calls the batch's builds made. It never
  exceeds `budget_units`. Each build in a batch still spends at most 80 units, and its cost
  also counts in its dossier's `spent_units`.
- When the budget would be exceeded by a further call, the batch makes no more provider calls,
  and its remaining builds complete with the pages and research claims they have obtained:
  each of their fields is `known` exactly when those support a value for it.

### `GET /batches/{id}`

Returns the batch in the shape above. `state` is `running` while any of its builds runs, then
`done`. Unknown batch is 404 `not_found`.

## Provider failure

A provider may answer a call with an error (any 5xx status, or 429). The build continues: it
may make the same request again, through that provider or another.

@[[42dcdeaf-6e11-4624-b620-7766b6084e53]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 3 of 3 (FINAL PART)


- A build in which every call to one or more providers fails, while `nimble` answers,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence (§4) reachable through the
  providers that answer supports.
- A build in which every research run fails, while searches and extracts are answered,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence reachable by search and
  extract supports.
- A build in which every call to every provider fails completes `failed` (§8), within the
  time bound of §8.
- A call a provider refuses with an error status costs nothing (§9).

## Restarts

The restart requirements of `stage-3.md` hold for batches as for the rest of the state. When
builds are running at the stop, everything else is still answered as before the stop, and
each build that was running:

- Does not stay `building`. It ends `ready` or `failed` within 10 seconds of `GET /health`
  first answering 200 after the restart, when each provider call it makes after the restart
  answers within one second. It may end `failed` although some of its calls succeeded; it
  then leaves the fields as they were (§8).
- Is one build across the restart: its calls before and after the stop together spend at
  most 80 units (§9), and a batch's builds together never spend more than its
  `budget_units`.
- Has every unit a provider billed for its calls, before and after the stop, counted in its
  dossier's `spent_units` and, for a batch's build, in the batch's `spent_units`. They may
  also count calls that were in flight at the stop and that no provider billed.

After the restart, `POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` starts a new build of each such dossier
as it does for any other.

## Upgrades

A stage-4 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3
service, preserving dossiers, candidates, history, the change feed and completed idempotent
responses as in `stage-1.md` §10. A stage-3 export keeps its
builds: after the upgrade, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer from them as the stage-3 service did,
with the keys this stage adds. Citations carried in the
imported state remain citations served to this service.

An export of a stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3 service has no `investors` candidates. After its
import, `investors` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the
export, and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it
adds a `change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes
`ready`.

**Files**
- `band-work/result/plans/stage-4-matrix.md`: 96 rows. F1–F88 are the new stage-4 requirements; F89–F96 are earlier-stage rules that stage 4 changes. It also records 12 decisions (D4-1 to D4-12).
- `band-work/result/plans/stage-4-plan.md`: 12 work items (U0–U11), with every row mapped to at least one. It also explains which provider calls each build makes and why each one can change a field.

**Main design choices**
- **Restarts:** a build still running when the service stops is recorded as `failed` at the next startup, before `/health` answers. It keeps the units it had already reserved. The spec allows this, and it spends nothing after the restart.
- **Spending:** units are reserved and written to the database before every provider call, so neither the 80-unit build cap nor a batch's budget can be exceeded, even across a crash.
- **Originals behind `Canonical` lines:** fetched only for pages that produced a candidate, at most three hops deep. Nimble stays the only provider.
- **Research failures:** a research run whose status checks keep failing is dropped after 3 failed checks, so the build still finishes within the 10-second bound. Today it can hang until the 270-second deadline.
- **Calls per build:** 10 cheap searches (one more than stage 3, for investors), then research, then page reads: research-cited pages first, then originals, then search results by priority until the cap. No search or page read repeats within a build. The plan does not stop early once fields look settled, because any unread page can still change a field's sources or status. The plan names the narrowest early stop if the lead wants one.

@[[b8d788a8-8bc7-49bc-9e05-1ca0d3dfc53a]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 1 of 3

# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

## Investors

A dossier has an eighth field, `investors`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after `executives`, and the feed entries one build adds are
numbered with `investors` last.

For Appendix A, `investors` is a field with the statement phrases `investor`, `investors`,
`led by`, `backed by` and `participated`. Occurrences of the company's name and of these
statement phrases are first taken out of the sentence and separate the words around them.
Of the runs of capitalised words (A.4) joined by single spaces that remain, each not part of
a longer such run, a run of two or more words whose last word is `Ventures`, `Capital`,

@[[b8d788a8-8bc7-49bc-9e05-1ca0d3dfc53a]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 2 of 3

`Partners`, `Fund`, `Investments`, `Holdings` or `Equity` is an **investor name**. In an
excerpt that contains an amount (A.4), the run that starts directly after `led by` or
`backed by` and one space is an investor name too, whatever its length and last word:
`Acme Robotics raised $40M in a round led by General Atlantic.` names `General Atlantic`,
and `Acme Robotics is led by Dana Ruiz.` names no investor. An
investor name normalises to the text as the excerpt writes it. Rules 1 to 4 of A.2 apply;
in place of rule 5, an excerpt supports each investor name it contains.

The `value` of a candidate of `investors` is one investor name. A research claim is never a
candidate of `investors`.

An investor name is a **member** when, among the field's candidates, one with that name has
`kind` `own` or `filing`, or those with that name have two or more distinct origins.

In place of the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, the value is the array of the members'
names, sorted by Unicode code point, or null when there is no member. `investors` is `known`
exactly when it has a member, and `unknown` otherwise, in place of the rules that make a
field `known` exactly when the evidence supports a value for it.

```json
{ "value": ["Bluebird Capital", "Northwind Ventures"], "status": "known",
  "true_from": "2024-05-02", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "candidates": [ { "value": "Bluebird Capital", "...": "...", "selected": true }, { "...": "..." } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "dealwire.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `selected` is true on every candidate whose name is a member, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate in the order the selection rule in `stage-2.md` ranks
  them.
- `citations` are, for each member in the order of the value, the `url`, `excerpt` and
  `provider` of every candidate with its name, in rank order.
- A member's `true_from` is the earliest `true_from` that is not null among the candidates
  with its name, or null when all of them are null. The field's `true_from` is the latest of
  its members' `true_from`, or null when the value is null or any member's is null.
- `GET /dossiers/{domain}/values` decides membership from the candidates at `true_at` and
  gives the value, `true_from` and `citations` from them by these rules.

A history and feed entry for `investors` is typed by name, in place of the table in
`stage-3.md` Changes and corrections. A name in the new value and not in the earlier one
counts as a correction when its `true_from` and the earlier value's `true_from` are both not
null and its `true_from` is on or before the earlier value's. The entry is `correction` when
every name in exactly one of the two values counts as a correction, and `change` otherwise.

The screens treat `investors` as `stage-3.md` treats `executives`: it takes none of the
`data-testid` attributes of `stage-2.md`, and "no field is contested" on `/contested` means
none of the six fields of §4 is.

## Batches

`POST /batches` starts builds, and so joins `POST /dossiers` and
`POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` as a request that makes provider calls (§8, Builds).

A batch researches several companies under one shared budget. A batch belongs to the user who
created it; another user's batch is 404 `not_found`.

### `POST /batches`

**An idempotent write path.** `Idempotency-Key` is required; see §7.

```http
POST /batches
Idempotency-Key: 5d02e1...

{ "domains": ["acme-robotics.test", "brightgear.test"], "budget_units": 200 }
```

```json
202
{ "batch_id": "b_2", "state": "running", "budget_units": 200, "spent_units": 0,
  "dossiers": [ { "domain": "acme-robotics.test", "state": "building" },
                { "domain": "brightgear.test", "state": "ready" } ] }
```

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| `domains` missing, empty or longer than 50 entries | 422 `validation_failed` |
| An entry of `domains` invalid after normalisation (§4) | 422 `validation_failed` |
| Two entries of `domains` the same after normalisation | 422 `validation_failed` |
| `budget_units` missing, not an integer, below 1 or above 100000 | 422 `validation_failed` |

A `budget_units` that is not an integer is 422 `validation_failed` whatever its JSON type: a
string, `true` or `1.5` included. The row above takes precedence over the 400
`malformed_request` of §5 for a field of the wrong JSON type.

- `dossiers` lists the normalised domains in the order given, each with its dossier's state.
- A domain with no dossier gets one, and the batch runs its first build. A domain that
  already has a dossier is not researched by the batch and costs it nothing.
- `spent_units` is the total cost (§9) of the provider calls the batch's builds made. It never
  exceeds `budget_units`. Each build in a batch still spends at most 80 units, and its cost
  also counts in its dossier's `spent_units`.
- When the budget would be exceeded by a further call, the batch makes no more provider calls,
  and its remaining builds complete with the pages and research claims they have obtained:
  each of their fields is `known` exactly when those support a value for it.

### `GET /batches/{id}`

Returns the batch in the shape above. `state` is `running` while any of its builds runs, then
`done`. Unknown batch is 404 `not_found`.

## Provider failure

A provider may answer a call with an error (any 5xx status, or 429). The build continues: it
may make the same request again, through that provider or another.

@[[b8d788a8-8bc7-49bc-9e05-1ca0d3dfc53a]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 3 of 3 (FINAL PART)


- A build in which every call to one or more providers fails, while `nimble` answers,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence (§4) reachable through the
  providers that answer supports.
- A build in which every research run fails, while searches and extracts are answered,
  completes `ready`, with every field `known` that the evidence reachable by search and
  extract supports.
- A build in which every call to every provider fails completes `failed` (§8), within the
  time bound of §8.
- A call a provider refuses with an error status costs nothing (§9).

## Restarts

The restart requirements of `stage-3.md` hold for batches as for the rest of the state. When
builds are running at the stop, everything else is still answered as before the stop, and
each build that was running:

- Does not stay `building`. It ends `ready` or `failed` within 10 seconds of `GET /health`
  first answering 200 after the restart, when each provider call it makes after the restart
  answers within one second. It may end `failed` although some of its calls succeeded; it
  then leaves the fields as they were (§8).
- Is one build across the restart: its calls before and after the stop together spend at
  most 80 units (§9), and a batch's builds together never spend more than its
  `budget_units`.
- Has every unit a provider billed for its calls, before and after the stop, counted in its
  dossier's `spent_units` and, for a batch's build, in the batch's `spent_units`. They may
  also count calls that were in flight at the stop and that no provider billed.

After the restart, `POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` starts a new build of each such dossier
as it does for any other.

## Upgrades

A stage-4 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3
service, preserving dossiers, candidates, history, the change feed and completed idempotent
responses as in `stage-1.md` §10. A stage-3 export keeps its
builds: after the upgrade, `?as_of=` and `/values` answer from them as the stage-3 service did,
with the keys this stage adds. Citations carried in the
imported state remain citations served to this service.

An export of a stage-1, stage-2 or stage-3 service has no `investors` candidates. After its
import, `investors` is `unknown`, in the imported state and in every build kept from the
export, and has no history entry; the first build that completes `ready` with a value for it
adds a `change`, or an `initial` entry when it is the dossier's first build that completes
`ready`.

# Dossier — Stage 1: company profiles

This stage defines the initial service and its API.

Build from the supplied requirements. Source code, API documentation and schemas from
existing products in this domain must not be used.
WebRouter's own documentation may be used.

## 1. Scope

A caller asks for a company by its web domain. The service researches the company on the web
and keeps a **dossier**: a profile of six fields, each with the value the web supports and the
excerpts it came from. A dossier is built in the background, read any number of times, and
refreshed on request. Only the HTTP API is required.

The following apply to all operations, including concurrent requests and retries:

1. Every value the service asserts cites at least one excerpt that a provider endpoint served
   to this service, and that excerpt supports the value. No citation is invented, reworded, or
   attached to a value it does not support.
2. No build of a dossier spends more than 80 units (§9).

Contact data, people search, and fields other than the six in §4 are out of scope.

## 2. Delivery and deployment

Deliver an HTTP service, a `Dockerfile` and a `RUN.md` with a command that builds and
starts the service without manual setup. Language, framework and storage are unrestricted.
A `docker-compose.yml` is optional.

The submission is a containerized HTTP service, not a Python package. Python is not
required in the implementation. TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, Python and any
other language are equally valid. The submitted `Dockerfile` is built and started,
and only its HTTP behavior is exercised; it does not import or execute the
submission's source files on the host that runs it.

The image must run on its own with `-e PORT=<port>` and a port mapping. All runtime
dependencies, initialization and seed data must work within that single container. Compose
configuration is not used to start the service.

### Web access

Two providers are available: `nimble` and `tavily`. Nimble is the default provider: every
service must be able to research companies using Nimble alone. Tavily is optional: a service
may use it beside Nimble, and its absence must not prevent research while Nimble answers.
The live submission and optional live judging provide a working Nimble key only.

The service reaches the providers only through WebRouter, the Python package `webrouter`
(module `web_router`). The service may be written in any language, but every request to a
provider goes through `web_router`: called in-process, or from a Python helper process that
the service runs inside its own container. The stage folder's dependency manifest lists
`webrouter>=0.12.0`. Calling a provider's API by any other route is not permitted.
Install it and the provider SDK dependencies from PyPI, including in the service's Docker build:

```sh
pip install "webrouter[search,extract,research]>=0.12.0"
```


The deployment provides these environment variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PORT` | The port to listen on (§3.1) |
| `NIMBLE_API_KEY` | Credential for the `nimble` provider |
| `NIMBLE_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `nimble` provider endpoint |
| `TAVILY_API_KEY` | Credential for the `tavily` provider |
| `TAVILY_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `tavily` provider endpoint |

Keys are opaque non-empty strings. WebRouter's `nimble` provider reads `NIMBLE_API_KEY` and
`NIMBLE_BASE_URL` from the environment, and its `tavily` provider reads `TAVILY_API_KEY`. A
service that uses Tavily passes its base URL to WebRouter in `provider_config`:

```python
provider_config={"tavily": {"api_base_url": <TAVILY_BASE_URL>}}
```

## Two times per value

Every candidate and every selected value now has two times:

- **`true_from`**: the date from which the evidence says the value holds. A page states it
  in the header line `Effective: <YYYY-MM-DD>`. A page with no valid `Effective` line takes
  the date part, in UTC, of its `published_at`; with neither, `true_from` is null.
- **`learned_at`**: when this service first had the value. For a candidate, it is the time

  and provider. For a selected value, it is the time of the build that made it the
  selected value.

Candidates gain `true_from` and `learned_at`. `retrieved_at` (stage 2) stays the time of the
build that gathered the candidate in the current candidate set. A selected value's
`true_from` is that of its selected candidate.

Each field of `GET /dossiers/{domain}` also carries the selected value's `true_from` and
`learned_at`. Both are null when the field is `unknown`. In an `as_of` response these
describe the selected value at that snapshot, using no later history.

A dossier has a seventh field, `executives`. The `fields` of every response that lists a

**members**. When no title has a selected person, the value is null and the field is

# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],

```

I've updated the stage-4 matrix and plan with the lead's six rulings and all the plan checker's findings, committed as `a6c1efeaaaccdf93a41063805d51ce6c0607a95a` on main. The lead and the checker both have the hash. I ran no code or checks.

**Lead's rulings, as now written in the plan**
- **Batch build stopped by the budget:** it ends `ready`, even with zero calls and every field unknown. The stage-4 batch text overrides the stage-1 failed rule only for budget exhaustion; a build whose calls all fail is still `failed`.
- **`/values`:** each field now also carries `origins` and `corroborated`, computed from the evidence on the requested date. `corroborated_since` is left out.
- **Wrong-typed `domains`:** still 400, while a bad `budget_units` is 422 whatever its type.
- **Spending:** no early stop once fields look settled, since any unread page can still change a field. Spend stays low because no search or page read repeats in a build and URLs that can't yield anything are never read. Originals are fetched only for pages that produced a value.
- **Restarts:** a call reserved but not yet answered at the stop counts as in flight. No reservation is held across any retry or poll wait.
- **10-second bound:** a new row (F97) and a timed schedule. With every provider call answering within 1 s, the worst case is:
  - searches and research start at 0–1 s, and research checks run 1–3 s;
  - research-cited pages are read at 3–4 s, and their originals take up to 3 hops at 4–7 s;
  - search-result pages are read from 4 s, and their originals take 5–8 s.

  No new call starts after 8.0 s, the cutoff the build code already uses. The last answer arrives by 9 s, so the build ends under 10 s. A research run still unfinished at 8 s is dropped, and a hop not started by then falls back to the URL's host.

**Checker's extra finding:** when a provider redirects, an original page is now judged by the URL it was actually served at, not the one requested. That covers whether it points to its…

1. D4-10: a zero-call batch build ends ready with all fields unknown. The matrix records that the Batches text overrides §8 for budget exhaustion only. A batch build whose calls all fail is still failed. The rule sits in one function, `build_outcome`, with tests for both cases.
2. D4-5: /values fields are now value, true_from, citations, origins and corroborated. The last two are computed from the candidates at true_at with the same member rules. No corroborated_since. Covered in F20, F50 and U8.
3. D4-9: kept.
4. Spend (F86, D4-13): no settled early stop. Spend stays minimal through call memos (by query, requested URL and served URL), no render of a URL that cannot yield a candidate or an original (duplicate, non-http(s), invalid host), and originals fetched only for pages with candidates. Proven by test_spend.py.
5. U7: in flight means from the reservation commit to the settle, and no reservation is held across any wait (D4-14).
6. Time bound: new row F97 and a schedule table in U5. A research run still unfinished at 8 s is dropped; a hop not started by 8 s uses the URL's host (DEV-S4b). Tests: worst_case_fast with every call answering in 0.95 s, and slow_research_fast_calls.

I also applied plan-checker's served-URL finding. The resolver's fetch now returns the URL the provider actually served together with the page's header lines. That served URL decides, for an original, the self-canonical test, the default registrant and the lookalike host (D4-16, with a redirect test).

Rows: F1-F97. All matrix and plan edits are in that commit; nothing is left open on my side. Still unverified: no code or checks run; a supplied check could still read D4-5, D4-9 or D4-10 differently; the fsync cost under load is unmeasured.

I fixed the timing error the plan checker raised in this second and last review cycle, committed as `7a30e10a4eb67f3a8361abf7a671045a231ea306`, and sent the checker the hash. Nothing was run; this is a plan change only.

**What was wrong:** the plan said a call with two retries takes at most 3.1 s. With provider answers taking up to 1 s, three attempts plus two waits take 1 + 1.05 + 1 + 1.05 + 1 = 5.1 s. Every step that waits on that call can shift up to 4.1 s later, so the timeline table in the plan could not prove the 10 s limit.

**What changed:**
- The timeline table (in both the plan and matrix row F97) is now labelled as the no-retry case and says it is not the bound.
- The 10 s proof now rests only on the cutoff rule: no attempt of any kind starts after 8.0 s of build time (time spent waiting after a 429 doesn't count). That covers retries, research checks, page reads and fetches of original pages. With answers within 1 s, every attempt ends by 9.0 s. Anything still waiting after 8.0 s re-checks the cutoff and gives up, and saving the result takes milliseconds, so the build ends under 10 s whatever the retries do.
- A new planned test, `mixed_retry_chain`, uses a fake provider answering every call in 0.95 s. In it, every search and the research start fail twice before succeeding, research status checks fail once, and original pages sit behind 3-hop chains with one refusal. It checks four things:
  - the build ends under 10 s with state `ready`;
  - no attempt starts after 8.0 s;
  - a hop cut off by the 8 s rule uses the URL's host;
  - only charged attempts count as spend.

This was the checker's last blocking issue, and the checker reports the final verdict to the lead. I haven't heard back yet. My note to the lead earlier this turn named the previous commit, `a6c1efe`, so they don't have this one from me.

## 10. Export and import

The service must support `GET /_test/export` and `POST /_test/import`. Like reset, these
are unauthenticated control endpoints.
Exports may contain credentials and session tokens; handle them as private artifacts.
Return 200 from export with a JSON object containing `track: "dossier"`,
`format_version: 1` and `state` (an implementation-defined JSON object). The state format
is opaque to the caller and must be accepted unchanged by import.

Import takes that entire object and atomically replaces the service's state, returning
204. It must accept an unchanged export produced by this service. No dependency on the
source process, files, volume, port or network address is allowed. Import is replacement,
not merge; repeating it restores the exported state without duplicating anything. Invalid
JSON follows §5; missing fields, wrong track/version or an invalid state give 422
`validation_failed` without changing the destination. These control calls have a 10-second
timeout. Export is an atomic, read-only snapshot; subsequent source writes do not change it.

Preserve accounts and hashed-password login, existing bearer tokens, dossiers with their
ids, states, fields, citations, `researched_at` and `spent_units`, all completed idempotent
request bodies and original responses. Identities and timestamps must not be regenerated.
Import makes no provider call: imported dossiers are not researched again, and their
citations remain citations served to this service. Failed request keys remain reusable.
Existing tokens and retries must remain valid after import; replacing the state with a fresh
front-end dependencies, and another developer can read it directly. The trade-off is that
DOM rendering is hand-written. To keep that manageable, each screen module exports
`render(state)` that builds DOM with a tiny `h(tag, attrs, children)` helper in `app.js`.

I fixed the plan checker's last blocking gap, which concerned budget for research-cited pages in batch builds. The fix is committed as `c2c12402b637ffebe1661ca4e3b21677796c378c` on main, and I've sent the checker the hash. Nothing was run; this is a plan change only.

**The gap:** the plan let a batch build start research (25 units) when only one extra page read (3 units) was affordable. Stage 2 requires reading every page a research claim cites. Research asks for six fields, so up to six pages may need reading at 3 units each, and the old rule could leave five of them unread.

**The fix (new matrix row F98):**
- Research starts only if 43 units (25 + 18) fit in both the build's own 80-unit cap and the batch budget, after the 10 searches.

- A hold is not a provider call. It never counts as spend, never appears in the spend saved for restart recovery, and never marks the batch budget as used up. If the hold doesn't fit, the build skips research and reads search pages instead.
- A build outside a batch always fits (80 − 10 = 70 units left). A batch build whose share is under 53 units skips research.
- A new planned test, `claim_reserve`, covers both sides of that line:
  - At a share of 53, research runs and all six cited pages are read.
  - At 52, research is skipped and nothing is left held.
  - A hold never shows up in spend.

@[[42dcdeaf-6e11-4624-b620-7766b6084e53]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 1 of 3

# Dossier — Stage 4: independent sources, batches and provider failure

All requirements from stages 1–3 continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4, §8 and §9 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

## Investors

A dossier has an eighth field, `investors`. The `fields` of every response that lists a
dossier's fields hold it, after `executives`, and the feed entries one build adds are
numbered with `investors` last.

For Appendix A, `investors` is a field with the statement phrases `investor`, `investors`,
`led by`, `backed by` and `participated`. Occurrences of the company's name and of these
statement phrases are first taken out of the sentence and separate the words around them.
Of the runs of capitalised words (A.4) joined by single spaces that remain, each not part of
a longer such run, a run of two or more words whose last word is `Ventures`, `Capital`,

@[[42dcdeaf-6e11-4624-b620-7766b6084e53]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 2 of 3

`Partners`, `Fund`, `Investments`, `Holdings` or `Equity` is an **investor name**. In an
excerpt that contains an amount (A.4), the run that starts directly after `led by` or
`backed by` and one space is an investor name too, whatever its length and last word:
`Acme Robotics raised $40M in a round led by General Atlantic.` names `General Atlantic`,
and `Acme Robotics is led by Dana Ruiz.` names no investor. An
investor name normalises to the text as the excerpt writes it. Rules 1 to 4 of A.2 apply;
in place of rule 5, an excerpt supports each investor name it contains.

The `value` of a candidate of `investors` is one investor name. A research claim is never a
candidate of `investors`.

An investor name is a **member** when, among the field's candidates, one with that name has
`kind` `own` or `filing`, or those with that name have two or more distinct origins.

In place of the selection rule in `stage-2.md`, the value is the array of the members'
names, sorted by Unicode code point, or null when there is no member. `investors` is `known`
exactly when it has a member, and `unknown` otherwise, in place of the rules that make a
field `known` exactly when the evidence supports a value for it.

```json
{ "value": ["Bluebird Capital", "Northwind Ventures"], "status": "known",
  "true_from": "2024-05-02", "learned_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "candidates": [ { "value": "Bluebird Capital", "...": "...", "selected": true }, { "...": "..." } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "dealwire.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `selected` is true on every candidate whose name is a member, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists every candidate in the order the selection rule in `stage-2.md` ranks
  them.
- `citations` are, for each member in the order of the value, the `url`, `excerpt` and
  `provider` of every candidate with its name, in rank order.
- A member's `true_from` is the earliest `true_from` that is not null among the candidates
  with its name, or null when all of them are null. The field's `true_from` is the latest of
  its members' `true_from`, or null when the value is null or any member's is null.

A provider may answer a call with an error (any 5xx status, or 429). The build continues: it
may make the same request again, through that provider or another.

@[[42dcdeaf-6e11-4624-b620-7766b6084e53]] spec stage-4 requirements, part 3 of 3 (FINAL PART)


- A build in which every call to one or more providers fails, while `nimble` answers,

  then leaves the fields as they were (§8).

  most 80 units (§9), and a batch's builds together never spend more than its
  `budget_units`.

  dossier's `spent_units` and, for a batch's build, in the batch's `spent_units`. They may

Many URLs can carry one source: copies, syndicated articles and lookalike domains. A dossier
now says which independent origins stand behind each value, and who has invested in the
company. Researchers submit companies in batches under one shared budget, and research
continues when provider calls fail. There are three idempotent write paths: stage 1's two
and `POST /batches`.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the earlier lists:

5. Spending never exceeds a budget that this specification or the caller sets.

## Lineage header lines

Three header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Registrant: <domain>` | The domain whose owner publishes the page |
| `Canonical: <URL>` | The page is a copy; the URL is the original |
| `First-Published-By: <domain>` | The page republishes material first published by that domain |

Domains in these lines, and the host of a `Canonical` URL, are normalised as in §4. A page
with no valid `Registrant` line has the host of its own URL, normalised, as its registrant.

## Own pages

A page counts as kind `own` for a company only when its registrant is the company's domain.
Any other page that states `Kind: own` has kind `aggregator` for the selection rule in
`stage-2.md`, and its candidates report `"kind": "aggregator"`.

A page that states `Kind: own` and whose registrant is not the host of its own URL,
normalised, is a **lookalike**: a site presenting itself as a company it is not registered
to.

## Origins

Every page has one **origin**, a domain, taken from the first of these that applies:

1. Its `First-Published-By` domain.
2. When its `Canonical` URL is not the page's own URL, the origin of the page at that URL
   (its **original**), by these same rules.
3. The company's domain, when the page is a lookalike.
4. Its registrant.

A build obtains from a provider each original that rule 2 needs. From the page whose origin
is sought, rule 2 follows at most three `Canonical` URLs in a row. Where it would follow a
fourth, or where no provider serves a page at the URL, the host of that URL takes the place
of the original's origin.

Pages with the same origin are one source, however many URLs, providers or kinds they have.

Candidates gain `origin`, the origin of their page. Each field gains three keys:

```json
{ "value": "Dana Ruiz", "status": "known",
  "citations": [ { "...": "..." } ], "candidates": [ { "...": "...", "origin": "acme-robotics.test" } ],
  "origins": ["acme-robotics.test", "registry.test"],
  "corroborated": true, "corroborated_since": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00" }
```

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates whose value is the selected value,
  sorted ascending. It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when `origins` has two or more entries, otherwise false.
- `corroborated_since` is the time (§8) of the earliest ready build after which the
  selected value has had two or more **standing origins**, or null while it has fewer.
  The standing origins of a selected value are the origins of every candidate with that
  value that any ready build has gathered since the value became the selected value (the
  `learned_at` of its latest history entry, stage 3), whether or not a later build
  gathered it again. A new selected value starts with none. Imported candidates count as
  gathered at the imported `researched_at`. When a stage-3 export is imported, the candidates
  of each of its builds count as gathered at that build's time.

Imported candidates whose export records no origin take the host of their URL, normalised,
as their origin.

For `executives` (`stage-3.md`) and `investors` (below), these keys follow the field's
members. A member's candidates are those with its title and name (`executives`) or with its
name (`investors`).

- `origins` lists the distinct origins of the candidates of all members, sorted ascending.
  It is `[]` for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated` is true when the candidates of every member have two or more distinct
  origins, and false otherwise, including for an `unknown` field.
- `corroborated_since` is the time of the earliest ready build after which every member has
  had two or more standing origins, or null while some member has fewer or the field is
  `unknown`. A member's standing origins are the origins of every candidate of that member
  that the build after which it last became a member, or any later ready build, has
  gathered, whether or not a later build gathered it again. Imported candidates count as
  above.

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess

import pytest

from conftest import (API, TEST_DOMAIN, create_build, feed, history, new_key,
                      parse_instant, refresh_build, wait_healthy)


def test_committed_state_survives_container_kill_and_start(api: API, token: str,
                                                            restart_container: str) -> None:
    """T67-T74: saved identities, dossier views, feed, idempotency and clock survive restart."""
    key = new_key()
    ready, initial = create_build(api, token, key=key)
    # Try for a feed entry; if the fixed corpus is unchanged, durability is still checked
    # against the existing history and feed snapshot.
    refreshed, _ = refresh_build(api, token)
    before_feed = feed(api, token)
    before = {
        "dossier": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}", token=token).json(),
        "as_of": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}?as_of={ready['researched_at']}",
                         token=token).json(),
        "values": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}/values?true_at=2099-12-31",
                          token=token).json(),
        "history": history(api, token, TEST_DOMAIN),
        "list": api.get("/dossiers", token=token).json(),
    }
    assert parse_instant(refreshed["researched_at"]) >= parse_instant(ready["researched_at"])
    subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", restart_container], check=True, capture_output=True,
                   text=True, timeout=30)
    subprocess.run(["docker", "start", restart_container], check=True, capture_output=True,
                   text=True, timeout=30)
    wait_healthy(api, timeout=90)

    # Existing token and password both remain usable.
    assert api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}", token=token).status_code == 200
    assert api.login()
    after = {
        "dossier": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}", token=token).json(),
        "as_of": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}?as_of={ready['researched_at']}",
                         token=token).json(),
        "values": api.get(f"/dossiers/{TEST_DOMAIN}/values?true_at=2099-12-31",
                          token=token).json(),
        "history": history(api, token, TEST_DOMAIN),
        "list": api.get("/dossiers", token=token).json(),
    }
    assert after == before
    assert feed(api, token) == before_feed
    replay = api.post("/dossiers", token=token, headers={"Idempotency-Key": key},
                      json={"domain": TEST_DOMAIN})
    assert replay.status_code == 200, replay.text
    assert replay.json() == initial.json()

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import pytest

from conftest import API, TEST_DOMAIN, create_build, wait_dossier


def test_build_budget_and_research_domain_search(mock_admin, api: API, token: str) -> None:
    """T75 and carried Stage 1/2 rules: provider spend is capped and exact search is singular."""
    if not mock_admin.enabled:
        pytest.skip("provider accounting needs DOSSIER_MOCK_URL and DOSSIER_MOCK_TOKEN")
    mock_admin.reset()
    dossier, _ = create_build(api, token, key="s3-budget-observable")
    calls = mock_admin.calls()
    assert sum(call["cost"] for call in calls) <= 80
    assert dossier["spent_units"] == sum(call["cost"] for call in calls)
    domain_searches = [call for call in calls if call.get("method") == "search"
                       and call.get("query") == TEST_DOMAIN and call["status"] < 400]
    assert len(domain_searches) == 1, domain_searches


def test_429_is_free_and_retried_after_rate_limit_interval(mock_admin, api: API,
                                                            token: str) -> None:
    """Carried Stage 1/2 ruling: three 429 retries, each spaced by at least one second."""
    if not mock_admin.enabled:
        pytest.skip("429 call accounting needs DOSSIER_MOCK_URL and DOSSIER_MOCK_TOKEN")
    mock_admin.reset()
    mock_admin.fault("nimble", ["search"], "rate_limit")
    domain = "stage3-rate-limit.test"
    response = api.post("/dossiers", token=token,
                        headers={"Idempotency-Key": "s3-rate-limit"},
                        json={"domain": domain})
    assert response.status_code == 202, response.text
    observed: dict[int, float] = {}
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 300
    calls = []
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        calls = [c for c in mock_admin.calls() if c.get("method") == "search"
                 and c.get("query") == domain and c.get("provider") == "nimble"]
        for count in range(1, len(calls) + 1):
            observed.setdefault(count, time.monotonic())
        if calls and calls[-1]["status"] < 400:
            break
        state_response = api.get(f"/dossiers/{domain}", token=token)
        if state_response.status_code == 200 and state_response.json()["state"] in ("ready", "failed"):
            break
        time.sleep(0.05)
    assert [call["status"] for call in calls] == [429, 429, 429, 200], calls
    assert all(call["cost"] == 0 for call in calls[:3])
    assert calls[3]["cost"] > 0
    assert all(observed[n + 1] - observed[n] >= 0.9 for n in (1, 2, 3)), observed


def test_non_429_refused_exact_domain_search_is_bounded_and_build_survives(
        mock_admin, api: API, token: str) -> None:
    """Carried Stage 1 rule: three exact-domain attempts; provider refusals cost nothing."""
    if not mock_admin.enabled:
        pytest.skip("provider refusal accounting needs DOSSIER_MOCK_URL and DOSSIER_MOCK_TOKEN")
    mock_admin.reset()
    mock_admin.fault("nimble", ["search"], "error")
    domain = "stage3-provider-refusal.test"
    response = api.post("/dossiers", token=token,
                        headers={"Idempotency-Key": "s3-provider-refusal"},
                        json={"domain": domain})
    assert response.status_code == 202, response.text
    dossier = wait_dossier(api, token, domain, timeout=120)
    assert dossier["state"] in ("ready", "failed")
    exact = [c for c in mock_admin.calls() if c.get("provider") == "nimble"

    assert 1 <= len(exact) <= 3, exact
    assert all(c["status"] >= 400 and c["cost"] == 0 for c in exact)

def test_committed_state_survives_kill_and_running_build_is_terminal(

        "dossier": api.get(f"/dossiers/{DOMAIN}", token=token).json(),
        "history": history(api, token),
        "feed": feed(api, token),
        "list": api.get("/dossiers", token=token).json(),
    }
    # Delay provider responses so batch builds are in flight when the container is killed.
    mock_admin.reset()
    mock_admin.delay("nimble", ["search"], 5)
    pending = api.post("/batches", token=token,
                       headers={"Idempotency-Key": key()},
                       json={"domains": ["restart-a.test", "restart-b.test"],
                             "budget_units": 100})
    assert pending.status_code == 202, pending.text
    batch_id = pending.json()["batch_id"]
    end = time.monotonic() + 10

            break
        time.sleep(0.05)
    assert any(call.get("method") == "search" for call in mock_admin.calls()), "no delayed provider call observed"
    subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", restart_container], check=True,

    subprocess.run(["docker", "start", restart_container], check=True,

    assert api.get(f"/dossiers/{DOMAIN}", token=token).status_code == 200
    assert api.login()
